title: Ella Langley's faith and authenticity fuel record-breaking rise, experts say
summary: Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" surpassed Mariah Carey and Whitney Houston records on the Billboard Hot 100, but her faith-driven rise is just beginning.
story: Country music superstar Ella Langley encouraged fans to not to measure themselves against social media or other people’s expectations during a concert performance.
Ella Langley is making music history without leaving behind the faith, values and traditional sound that first won over fans.

The 27-year-old country star's song "Choosin' Texas" has hit the No. 1 spot on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for the 15th nonconsecutive week, surpassing Mariah Carey's 2005 R&B classic "We Belong Together" and Whitney Houston's iconic 1992 power ballad "I Will Always Love You," both of which spent 14 weeks atop the chart, according to a report published by Billboard on Monday.

Langley became the first solo female artist to top the Billboard Hot 100 for that long with a non-holiday song. Mariah Carey's perennial 1994 holiday hit, "All I Want for Christmas Is You," is the only song by a solo female singer to spend more time at No. 1, with 22 weeks atop the chart.
ELLA LANGLEY'S 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SPENDS 15 WEEKS AT NUMBER ONE ON THE BILLBOARD HOT 100
The milestone is the latest achievement in a breakout year that has transformed Langley into one of country music's biggest success stories.
Ella Langley is making music history without abandoning her roots. (SXSW Conference & Festivals via Getty Images)

Beyond the charts, Langley won major industry awards and has expanded her mainstream profile through high-profile brand partnerships, television appearances and recognition from some of country music's most influential artists.
Born in Hope Hull, Alabama, Langley left her hometown in 2019 to move to Nashville, Tennessee, where she spent years writing songs, touring and building a loyal following online.

Langley made her breakthrough with her Riley Green duet "You Look Like You Love Me," which went viral on TikTok, amassed millions of streams on Spotify and Apple Music and introduced her to a wider audience.
The country star's song "Choosin' Texas" has topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 15 nonconsecutive weeks. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
COUNTRY MUSIC STAR RILEY GREEN FIRES UP FANS WITH EPIC NEW SUMMER JAM 'THINK AS YOU DRUNK'

Since then, Langley has emerged as one of country music's most recognizable faces, pairing record-setting commercial success with growing mainstream visibility. The singer recently launched an American Eagle campaign and earned praise from icons, including Shania Twain.
Throughout her rise, Langley has continued to publicly discuss her Christian faith and Alabama upbringing while releasing music firmly rooted in traditional country.
Advertisement
She has frequently thanked God during award speeches, and last month went viral for passionate remarks about faith, Christianity and love during a concert in Lexington, Kentucky.
Langley recently landed a campaign with American Eagle. (Getty Images for American Eagle Outfitters)
While speaking with Rolling Stone last week, Twain described Langley as an "authentic songwriter."
SHANIA TWAIN CALLS ELLA LANGLEY AN 'AUTHENTIC SONGWRITER' WITH A UNIQUE SOUND IN NEW INTERVIEW
"She sounds original," Twain said. "She really does seem very unapologetic."
"That commands respect," Twain added. "I believe what she's saying."

Music and branding experts say those qualities may help explain why Langley has resonated with audiences far beyond country music and why her rise comes at a time when country has become one of America's dominant musical genres.
Shania Twain praised Langley as an "authentic songwriter" and "unapologetic." (Matthew Baker/Getty Images for ABA)
Veteran country music journalist Marcus K. Dowling told Fox News Digital that Langley's appeal isn't a departure from country music's traditions but rather an extension of them.

"Country music has proven that, more often than not, when music, above all else, is rooted in a strong sense of faith, family and fun, it appeals to a lowest and middle common denominator of Americans better than most any other stereotypical American thing," Dowling said.

"Look at the back to back to back moment for Langley," he continued. "It's a tale of how to break a star in on country that's as old as the genre is: A duet with a more established male performer. A discovery, by the genre's fanbase, that her authentically rooted musicality is real, and pairs well with her spotlight-ready cosmetic appeal."

"Then, a song that ties a female performer to an emotive core defined by lovestruck universal yearnings," he added. "From Patsy Cline singing ‘Crazy’ through to Dolly and ‘Jolene,’ Gretchen. Wilson's ‘Redneck Woman’ and more, what Ella's doing has a long lineage of always working when executed with intentionality, honesty, and precision."
Langley made her breakthrough with her Riley Green duet "You Look Like You Love Me." (Theo Wargo/Getty Images)
Doug Eldridge, founder of Achilles PR, said Langley's success also reflects what audiences are increasingly looking for in entertainers.

"Humility and self-deprecation go a long way when it comes to connecting with fans," Eldridge said. "In the end, authenticity is a lot like humidity — you can’t see it, but you can feel it; when you do, it’s undeniable."
"Langley has humidity and people embrace that," he added. "At this point, that’s what most of us want: real."
Dowling told Fox News Digital that he believes Langley's rise is emblematic of a broader resurgence that has propelled country music to its greatest level of mainstream popularity in decades.

"We haven't seen country be this pop-dominant in 40 years, dating back to Dolly Parton, Kenny Rogers and the like achieving initial mainstream moments that were almost entirely couched in a very stereotypical brand of blending the Appalachian and Western aesthetics with what, ultimately, country had become as a repository for really great, crossover-friendly pop music," he said.
Langley has continued to frequently speak out about her faith. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
Eldridge argued that country's recent dominance is not surprising because its songs often center on universal experiences.

"Most of the artists are singing about topics that the majority of Americans can relate to: loving your family, being proud of your country, first love, lost love, struggling with bills, trying to be a better person, and giving thanks to Jesus," he said.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"This has been the foundational basis for American vision, values and virtues for a long time," Eldridge added. "Others are just waking up to that reality."
Langley's growing mainstream appeal has drawn comparisons to Taylor Swift's crossover from her country music beginnings to global pop stardom.
However, Eldridge pointed to what he views as a key difference between the two artists.
The singer's rise has drawn comparisons to Taylor Swift's early career crossover. (Andre Dias Nobre/AFP via Getty Images)
"Langley is more true to country music, than Swift ever was in her early days," Eldridge said. "That said, Swift built an audience — and later, an empire — so she knew what she was doing all along."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Eldridge told Fox News Digital that it is too early to know whether Langley will ultimately follow Swift's trajectory or reach the same level of commercial success. He also pointed out that Swift is far from the first country-pop crossover star.

"Swift deserves all the credit for her self-built, billion-dollar empire, but assigning her sole attribution for the country-pop cross-over is looking past all those artists who successfully built that model and passed down the blueprint," he said.
PR expert Doug Eldridge said Langley should stick to her roots rather than pursue a full pop crossover. (Ethan Miller/Reuters)
Eldridge argued Langley may be better served by continuing to lean into the country sound and faith-based identity that have defined her career rather than pursuing a full-fledged pop crossover.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Langley has both commercial appeal and a sense of authenticity — it’s hard to maintain both once you fully commit to the pop cross-over," he said.
"Historically speaking, country artists have careers; pop artists have a moment."
Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

title: Zac Brown Band's John Driskell Hopkins says he's 'chasing the clock' after ALS diagnosis
summary: John Driskell Hopkins says he's "chasing the clock" since his 2021 ALS diagnosis, still touring with Zac Brown Band while planning for 2027.
story: John Driskell Hopkins told Fox News Digital that he's been trying to fit in as much as possible since his diagnosis in 2021.
Zac Brown Band's John Driskell Hopkins is opting to look at his ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) diagnosis in a different light and is trying to make everyday count.

Over a decade after the Ice Bucket Challenge surfaced on social media, it is making a comeback. During an interview with Fox News Digital about the challenge, Hopkins explained that after his diagnosis in 2021, he's been "chasing the clock" ever since.

"I'm almost busier now than I was before because I'm trying to get so much done. I'm tryin' to fit it all in. I'm taking more family vacations. I'm in the studio more than I should be. I'm still on tour with Zac Brown Band right now. You know, my fingers work. My voice works, it's been compromised, but most of the set, no one would notice," Hopkins, a founding member of Zac Brown Band, said.
John Driskell Hopkins of Zac Brown Band was diagnosed with ALS in 2021. (Derek White/Getty Images for The Recording Academy)

He continued, "And I'm playing different things on stage, but they still don't make sense. You know, I'm chasing the clock more than I ever have been. And what I worry about is that that is causing me stress, which might be exacerbating my condition. So it's a bit of a catch-22, you know, I've created."
ZAC BROWN BAND'S JOHN DRISKELL HOPKINS FIGHTS ALS DIAGNOSIS: ‘CRYING SUCKS’
Acknowledging the reality of his diagnosis, Hopkins said that he's looking toward the future where he might not be able to sing.
"I hope that my progression continues to be slow and that I can sing for a long time, but who knows?" he said.

In 2014, Hopkins and the Zac Brown Band participated in the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge on social media – years before his diagnosis. At the time, Hopkins had no idea what the disease was, let alone that he would be diagnosed one day.
"I'm chasing the clock more than I ever have been."
WATCH: Zac Brown Band's John Driskell Hopkins is 'chasing the clock' after ALS diagnosis

"I didn't even know what it was. I mean, I think a lot of people in the band that did the challenge with me understood that it was neurological and fatal, but we didn't have any clue as to how it affected the body more," he began.

"Certainly not how cases were increasing. I mean, we have seen an explosion of neurodegenerative diseases and I can only, generally point to maybe its toxicity. You know, maybe in the world where we're just consuming a lot more things that are doing us harm. That's all I can guess. But I would have never thought… I was indestructible in 2014, you know?"

With several notable public figures recently diagnosed with ALS, the Ice Bucket Challenge has begun resurfacing across social media. Hop and his team at Hop On A Cure have now joined in, sharing their own Ice Bucket Challenge video and passing the challenge on to fellow ALS organizations, as well as the Zac Brown Band.
MICHAEL J. FOX SAYS GOING PUBLIC WITH PARKINSON'S WAS 'HELL' ON WIFE TRACY POLLAN

Hopkins told Fox News Digital he's glad the trend has come back around this summer. Hopkin's nonprofit organization and the Zac Brown Band posted videos on Instagram in July participating in the challenge.
"It's very popular, and it's fun in the summer. It's been a really hot summer this year, all over the world. And we were in London with 95 degree days, and they never see that," Hopkins said.
John Driskell Hopkins and wife Jennifer started the nonprofit, Hop On a Cure, in 2022. (Emilee Chinn/Cincinnati Reds)
When asked how he's been able to stay strong during his diagnosis, Hopkins told Fox News Digital that he doesn't feel strong at all.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I don't feel strong, people often ask me where my strength comes from, but I feel incredibly weak, not just physically. You know, I'm an actor, I have a theater degree, so I'm acting strong," he said.
WATCH: John Driskell Hopkins talks about the viral ALS Ice Bucket Challenge

Hopkins was diagnosed with ALS just before Christmas in 2021 and announced his diagnosis in May 2022. After his diagnosis, Hopkins and his wife, Jennifer, founded the nonprofit organization, Hop On A Cure, to help accelerate research to prevent, reverse and ultimately cure ALS while also raising awareness and supporting families affected by the disease.
At the time of his diagnosis, Hopkins emphasized that his disease had been slowly progressing, allowing him to continue touring and performing with the band.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
During his interview with Fox News Digital, Hopkins said he's in a different position than 99% of ALS patients because he is still able to plan for the next calendar year.
John Driskell Hopkins feels fortunate to still be planning for 2027 amid his ALS diagnosis. (ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty Images)

"The fact that I still see next year in my future puts me in a different position than 99.9% of ALS patients. The fact that I'm looking to my calendar for '27. I'm gonna be at the 30a Songwriters Festival '27, and maybe I won't be able to sing what I can now, but maybe I will, you know, we just don't know, and I appreciate you recognizing that reaction as strength, but to me, it's getting up every day that I can and doing what I do," Hopkins concluded.

title: George and Amal Clooney evacuate France home as wildfires spread across Europe
summary: George and Amal Clooney sent a letter to the Brignoles mayor before evacuating, saying they have "no idea" if their home will survive the fires.
story: Wildfires are sweeping across Spain and France, forcing more than 250,000 people to evacuate. One blaze is threatening France's famed Bordeaux wine region, while Spain has declared a national emergency. France has deployed the military, and the Tour de France has been shortened as firefighters battle the massive blazes.
A representative for George Clooney confirmed the evacuation to People and shared a letter the couple sent to Brignoles Mayor Didier Brémond

The couple and their 9-year-old twins left their home in Brignoles, in France's Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region, as fires threatened large swaths of the Mediterranean, the outlet reported. A representative for George Clooney confirmed to People that the couple sent a letter to Brignoles Mayor Didier Brémond before leaving.
"Dear Didier, At this point we have no idea whether our beautiful home makes it through this terrible moment," the letter began.
DEADLY FRENCH WILDFIRES THREATEN MISSILE PLANTS, NUCLEAR SITES AS FOURTH HEATWAVE LOOMS
George and Amal Clooney reportedly evacuated their home in southern France as fast-moving wildfires spread across parts of Europe. (Joe Maher; AP Photo/Emma Da Silva)

"As we evacuate Brignoles we want to emphasise 2 things, first we hope you and the people of our city are safe and second that Amal and i are committed to making sure that whatever happens to our village, we are part of this community and we’ll be part of making it whole," the letter continued. "We love Brignoles and our friends who live there."
Fox News Digital has reached out to Clooney's representatives for additional comment, including whether the family has safely evacuated and if there is any update on the condition of their home.
The evacuation comes as wildfires continue to scorch southern Europe.
EUROPE'S FIRES REVEAL DEADLY MIX OF RECORD HEAT, HUMAN ERROR, ARSON AND LAND MISMANAGEMENT
George and Amal Clooney reportedly left their home in Brignoles, France, as wildfires spread across the region, according to People. (Paul Morigi/Getty Images for History)

As of Wednesday, an uncontained wildfire roughly four times the size of Paris was burning across southwestern France.  The blaze was separate from the fire threatening the Brignoles area, where about 3,000 people were evacuated. Fires also continued to threaten parts of southern Europe, and three firefighters died in Greece as crews battled extreme heat, drought and strong winds, according to The Associated Press.
More than 300,000 people have been forced to evacuate in France and Spain, including residents and tourists.

Temperatures climbed to nearly 104 degrees Wednesday in France's Gironde region, where the country's largest wildfire prompted the evacuation of roughly 220,000 residents and vacationers at its peak. While many have since returned, tens of thousands remain displaced.
HEATHER LOCKLEAR SAYS SHE LIVES 'FAR AWAY' FROM HOLLYWOOD AND STAYS OUT OF THE SOCIAL SCENE
Clooney and his family spend much of their time on a farm in France. (Christopher Anderson/Esquire)
In an October 2025 interview with Esquire , Clooney said he and Amal chose to raise their family on a farm in France to give their children a quieter upbringing away from Hollywood.

"A good portion of my life growing up was on a farm, and as a kid, I hated the whole idea of it," he said. "But now, for them, it’s like—they’re not on their iPads, you know? They have dinner with grown-ups and have to take their dishes in. They have a much better life."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Clooney also said he was "worried about raising our kids in L.A., in the culture of Hollywood."

"I felt like they were never going to get a fair shake at life," he said. "France — they kind of don’t give a s--- about fame. I don’t want them to be walking around worried about paparazzi. I don’t want them being compared to somebody else’s famous kids."

title: Megan Moroney cancels show mid-performance, leaves stage in tears
summary: Megan Moroney called canceling her Denver concert at Ball Arena "the hardest decision" she's ever made. The show is rescheduled for Aug. 27.
story: Country music star Megan Moroney told Fox News Digital she is not ‘emotionally available’ for a romantic relationship, putting all her energy into her music career.
Country star Megan Moroney cut her Denver concert short Tuesday night after becoming too sick to continue performing, later telling fans it was "the hardest decision" she has ever had to make.
The singer took the stage at Ball Arena but struggled through just three songs before stopping the show. Moroney returned to address the audience herself, apologizing as she fought back tears.
"I am obviously extremely sick, and I thought I did everything to make myself better, and obviously, two songs in, I just can't play this show tonight," she told the crowd in a fan-recorded video.
JON BON JOVI ABRUPTLY ENDS MADISON SQUARE GARDEN SHOW AFTER HEALTH SETBACK
Fan-recorded video captures Megan Moroney fighting back tears as she stops her Denver Ball Arena show after just three songs due to illness. (Photo by Rick Kern/Getty Images for CMT)
MEGAN MORONEY STUNS IN ORANGE BIKINI DURING FRIEND'S BAHAMAS BACHELORETTE
Despite ending the performance early, Moroney assured concertgoers she planned to make up for the disappointing night.
"I want to give you guys the show you deserve. ... I'm sorry," she said.
Fans inside the arena responded with encouragement, with one audience member shouting, "That's OK Meg, I love you," as the visibly emotional singer exited the stage.
Ball Arena later confirmed the concert had been canceled because Moroney was feeling under the weather.
The "Am I Okay?" singer shared an emotional Instagram message after ending her concert early, promising Denver fans a rescheduled date. (NDZ/Star Max/GC Images)
"Megan is unable to continue her performance this evening due to illness, and we must end the show at this time," the venue said in a statement.
"Please allow event staff to direct you to the nearest exit, and we will follow up with more information as soon as we're able."
COUNTRY SINGER MEGAN MORONEY SWEARS OFF DATING AFTER MEN 'RUINED' HER BIGGEST MOMENTS
Moroney apologized to fans for canceling her Denver show, saying she was unable to perform at 100% and announcing the concert has been rescheduled. (Megan Moroney/Instagram)
The venue added that updates would be posted on its website and apologized "for the inconvenience" while thanking fans for their understanding and cooperation.
Shortly after, Moroney shared an emotional message with fans on Instagram, explaining that continuing the concert would have meant delivering a performance below her own standards.
"That was the hardest decision I've ever had to make & I'm so sorry to cancel the show tonight," she wrote.

"I never ever will give you guys a show that is not 100% and by song 3 I knew that I was not capable of giving that to you tonight."
The "Am I Okay?" singer said she was devastated by the decision, adding, "I'm typing this as I'm quite literally bawling my eyes out in my dressing room & it hurts me so much to disappoint you all."

Moroney also announced that the Denver concert has been rescheduled for Aug. 27. Tickets purchased for Tuesday night's performance will be honored for the new date, and fans unable to attend can request refunds through their original point of purchase.
"I've never had to do this & I'm truly so sorry," she wrote before closing her message with, "i love u guys."
Fox News Digital reached out to Moroney for comment.

After leaving college, she moved to Nashville. Moroney's "Tennessee Orange" breakthrough helped transform her into an award-winning country sensation. (John Shearer/Getty Images for CMT)
The abrupt cancellation comes as Moroney continues touring following the success of her third album and a string of sold-out performances across the country.
Her emotional apology and promise to return were met with widespread support from fans online, many of whom encouraged the singer to focus on recovering before getting back on stage.
Despite the canceled show, Moroney's music career continues to soar.
After attending the University of Georgia, she moved to Nashville to pursue music full time.

GISELE BÜNDCHEN CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY IN LEOPARD-PRINT BIKINI AS SHE REFLECTS ON GRATITUDE

title: Willie Nelson urges Americans to fight 'water thieving' AI data centers devouring rural Texas farmland
summary: Willie Nelson urges Americans to fight data centers invading rural Texas land, warning of light pollution and water thieving near his Abbott home.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Willie Nelson urged Americans to think again when it comes to building the future.
Nelson, 93, encouraged followers to "fight against data centers invading our land" in a social media plea shared Tuesday.
The country music legend reflected on being able to see "stars at night" in his Texas hometown, but that light pollution and "water thieving" were imminent in a looming industrial climate.
KACEY MUSGRAVES ABRUPTLY CANCELS CONCERT DATES FROM 'MIDDLE OF NOWHERE' TOUR
Willie Nelson pleaded with his followers Tuesday to focus on the environmental impacts of data farming centers. (Peter Pakvis)
"I grew up in Abbott, and I still have a home there with farmed land where I can still see stars at night," Nelson told his followers.
"And now our community, like many others, needs to fight against data centers invading our land.
SINGER ZACH TOP SLAMS MODERN COUNTRY MUSIC, SAYS IT LACKS 'SOUL'
"The last thing we need is a loud, water thieving, light polluting, data center anywhere near our town (or any others for that matter)."
The "On the Road Again" singer noted how "the strength of rural America has never come from big industrial footprints."
A post shared by Willie Nelson (@willienelsonofficial)

"It comes from generations of people, open spaces, local businesses, and a connection to the land," Nelson wrote. "All of America deserves thoughtful stewardship that doesn’t steal farmland (where our essential shared-food is grown) and small family farmers’ livelihoods, and not data centers that only destroy the environment around them.

"Whoever controls food and water, controls the masses. Let’s not allow our own demise or give up control over necessary resources in the U.S. and especially in Abbott."
The legendary country singer reflected on the need for "thoughtful stewardship that doesn't steal farmland." (Rick Kern)
Nelson's a longtime environmental advocate and has raised more than $90 million through his Farm Aid nonprofit, which he co-founded with John Mellencamp and Neil Young more than four decades ago.
The charity was first formed in 1985 to raise awareness about the loss of family farms and to raise funds to keep farm families on the land.
On Tuesday, Gov. Greg Abbott called for a ban on data center developments in rural Texas.

"We must prohibit them from building AI data centers in rural Texas neighborhoods," he said on a campaign stop in Bullard, according to The Texas Tribune.
Willie Nelson has raised more than $90 million through his Farm Aid nonprofit, which he founded in 1985 with John Mellencamp and Neil Young. (Gary Miller)

"I made clear already: Any AI data center even thinking about coming here — they got to bring their own money, bring their own power, reuse their own water and do it in a way that reduces the cost of electricity for residents across our state.

"We must eliminate the tax break they are getting. They must be responsible for funding their own projects here in Texas. We will get that done."

title: Jared Leto responds to sexual misconduct allegations made by multiple women in explosive documentary
summary: Jared Leto denies sexual assault allegations from four women who claim offenses occurred when they were teenagers, calling the claims "categorically false."
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Jared Leto is denying allegations of criminal sexual conduct after four women accused the Oscar-winning actor and musician of offenses they claim occurred when they were teenagers.
"I have never sexually assaulted anyone in my entire life," Leto said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. "These claims are absolutely and categorically false."

The allegations are detailed in the new BBC documentary, "Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret," which premiered Wednesday. The film features interviews with 10 participants, nine of whom shared their stories publicly for the first time.
According to the documentary, four women allege Leto engaged in criminal sexual conduct between 2002 and 2016, when the actor and Thirty Seconds to Mars frontman — now 54 — was in his 30s and 40s.
JASON ALEXANDER APOLOGIZES AFTER COURTNEY STODDEN SAYS 2012 COMEDY SKETCH OBJECTIFIED HER AS A MINOR
Jared Leto has denied allegations of sexual misconduct, telling Fox News Digital the claims are "categorically false." (Christopher Polk/Variety via Getty Images)

In a BBC story published Wednesday, one woman alleged she had sex with Leto at his California home when she was 17 years old. According to the outlet, the woman said Leto, who was 34 at the time, dismissed concerns after they discussed California's age of consent being 18.
"It wasn't a huge concern for him," she alleged. "He told me, 'I would like you to call me daddy.' And it was either pretend to be a little girl or 'my little girl.'"
The woman said that because she was "so naive and vulnerable" at the time, she didn't understand that this behavior wasn't "normal" in an adult relationship.
"It was only as time went on that I realized more and more how scary that really was," she said.
OSCAR WINNER JARED LETO ADMITS DEPTHS OF DRUG ADDICTION: 'IT TOOK ME FOR A RIDE'
A second woman alleged Leto sexually assaulted her in what she described as a "dingy gross motel" in Las Vegas in 2002, saying he invited her there after meeting her at the store where she worked.
According to the documentary, the woman said Leto called her into the bathroom while he was showering.
Multiple women have alleged sexual misconduct against Leto, four of whom were teens at the time.  (Mike Marsland/WireImage)
"I don't think there was many words exchanged, and he opened the shower curtain and started kissing me," she alleged.
She claimed Leto then grabbed her hand and forced her to masturbate him.
"Most of my life I had viewed this event as, I was a stupid girl … and so this bad thing happened," she said.
A third woman alleged Leto threatened her with sexual assault after inviting her to a hotel room in London after a Thirty Seconds to Mars concert in 2013.

The former model said she was 19 at the time but told Leto she was 17 because she "felt the need" to pretend to be younger to protect herself. After telling Leto she was 17, the woman claimed he said, "Age is just a number, and, anyway, we're in Europe."
JARED LETO RECALLS ‘NEARLY DYING’ WHILE ROCK CLIMBING
The woman claimed one of Leto's assistants encouraged her to join in on another party at a nearby hotel room. However, when she arrived, she realized there was no party.
Ten participants spoke about their experiences with Leto in a new BBC documentary.  (Jason Kempin/Getty Images for MTV)
"I get into the hotel room, it's really dark and then I see that it's just him," she said. "Weren't there supposed to be other people?"
The woman claimed she asked Leto for a phone charger or some cash to get home, but he dismissed her requests.

After asking if she could sleep on a chaise lounge because she had no way home, the woman claimed Leto repeatedly told her she would wake up "with a d--- in her ass."
After realizing she "was not safe," the woman left the room.
A fourth woman said Leto began grooming her when she was 16, made repeated sexually explicit phone calls to her and on at least one occasion suggested the two have sex.

According to the BBC, the woman was later presented with a nondisclosure agreement intended to prevent her from discussing her alleged relationship with Leto. She declined to sign the document, which BBC said it had reviewed.
Leto reportedly did not respond to requests for comment during the making of the documentary. (Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic)
Additional women also accused the actor of making what they described as "strange" and sexually explicit phone calls while they were underage or teenagers.

The documentary also featured interviews with two former employees connected to Thirty Seconds to Mars, who claim staff members were uncomfortable with Leto's interactions with teenage girls.
One former employee alleged Leto would invite teenage girls backstage to his dressing room or to a house where the band was recording.
"I think everyone thought the age gap was way too big," the former employee said.
The allegations are the latest in a series of claims against the Academy Award winner.

In June 2025, Air Mail published interviews with nine women who alleged Leto engaged in inappropriate sexual behavior over the years, including accusations involving minors. Those allegations included claims that Leto asked sexually explicit questions to a 16-year-old, exposed himself to a 17-year-old and placed an 18-year-old's hand "on him."
The Thirty Seconds to Mars frontman was in his 30s and 40s at the time of the alleged allegations.  (Lia Toby/Getty Images)
The Air Mail report followed allegations by Los Angeles DJ Allie Teilz, who publicly claimed she was assaulted by Leto when she was 17.
At the time, representatives for Leto "expressly" denied the Air Mail allegations, calling Teilz's claims "demonstrably false."

title: Oscar-winning singer Glen Hansard dead at 56
summary: Glen Hansard, the Oscar-winning Irish singer-songwriter behind "Falling Slowly" and star of "Once," died at 56 in a motorcycle crash in Dublin.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard, the Academy Award-winning musician behind the beloved song "Falling Slowly" and star of the acclaimed film "Once," has died after a motorcycle crash in Dublin. He was 56.
Hansard's management confirmed his death Wednesday, telling Irish broadcaster RTÉ that his family was "deeply shocked and heartbroken."

According to Irish police, a man in his 50s was killed in a single-vehicle motorcycle crash in Lucan, on the outskirts of Dublin, before 4:30 a.m. Wednesday. First responders treated the rider at the scene, but he was pronounced dead shortly after.
'IT TAKES TWO' RAPPER ROB BASE DEAD AT 59 AFTER CANCER FIGHT HE KEPT HIDDEN FROM FRIENDS
Glen Hansard died after a motorcycle crash on July 29. (Luciano Viti/Getty Images)
Hansard's legacy was tied to "Once," the 2007 Irish musical drama that transformed him from a respected hometown musician into an international star.
Starring opposite Markéta Irglová, Hansard played a struggling street musician whose connection with a fellow artist unfolds through music on the streets of Dublin.
The film became a global success, earning roughly $23 million at the worldwide box office and producing one of the decade's most memorable original songs, according to Rolling Stone.
GEORGE MICHAEL DIED WORTH $128M, BUT FRIENDS SAY HE SECRETLY GAVE AWAY MILLIONS FOR DECADES: AUTHOR
Hansard was best known for starring in "Once," which contained the Oscar-winning song "Falling Slowly." (Luciano Viti/Getty Images)
Hansard and Irglová won the Academy Award for best original song in 2008 for "Falling Slowly," a quiet acoustic ballad that became synonymous with the film.
Long before Hollywood recognition, Hansard had already established himself as one of Ireland's most respected performers.
Born in Ballymun, Dublin, in 1970, he began playing music as a teenager while busking throughout the city.

In 1990, he founded The Frames, a band that developed a devoted following over several decades. Around the same time, Hansard expanded into acting, appearing as guitarist Outspan Foster in Alan Parker's 1991 film "The Commitments."
His career continued to evolve after "Once." Alongside Irglová, he formed The Swell Season while also maintaining an active solo career.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Markéta Irglová and Glen Hansard of The Swell Season are seen performing during the 2025 Newport Folk Festival. (Douglas Mason/Getty Images)
His 2015 album "Didn't He Ramble" earned a Grammy nomination for Best Folk Album.
Hansard was equally recognized for the way he remained connected to Dublin's music community despite his international success.

Each Christmas Eve, he gathered fellow musicians outside Dublin's Gaiety Theatre for a charity busking tradition benefiting the Dublin Simon Community, an annual event that became a holiday fixture for locals.
He also played a prominent role during one of Ireland's most emotional public farewells.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

At the funeral of Pogues frontman Shane MacGowan in December 2023, Hansard and Irish singer Lisa O'Neill performed "Fairytale of New York," inspiring mourners throughout the church to sing and dance in celebration of MacGowan's life.
Hansard's reputation reached well beyond Ireland.
Hansard is seen performing at Michael Dorf Presents: The Music Of Van Morrison at Carnegie Hall on March 21, 2019, in New York City. (Bobby Bank/Getty Images)
The Irish musician joined Bruce Springsteen onstage at Kilkenny's Nowlan Park in 2013 for a performance of "Drive All Night."
Tributes from across Ireland began pouring in within hours of news of his death.
Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin wrote on X that he was "deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Glen Hansard."
"A talented musician and actor who made a significant contribution to Ireland's cultural landscape over many years," Martin posted.

Waterboys frontman Mike Scott also reflected on Hansard's legacy, writing on X, "Just heard that Glen Hansard has died. Travel on well, Buddy. You made your dreams come true. I'm so sorry that he leaves his wife and 3-year-old child."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Hansard is survived by his partner, Finnish poet Maire Saaritsa, and their son, Christy, who was born in 2022.
His career leaves behind a catalog that stretched from Dublin sidewalks to the Oscar stage, making him one of Ireland's most enduring musical voices.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: King Charles sends 'defiance' message to Prince William with Buckingham Palace room offer to Harry: expert
summary: Royal experts say Prince William demands hard boundaries with Prince Harry while King Charles seeks healing, creating a rift over the monarchy's future.
story: Dan Wakeford, founder of Celebrity Intelligence, discusses Prince Harry's expected UK return, his relationship with King Charles, and why a meeting with Prince William remains unlikely.
King Charles and his heir are said to be at odds over how to handle Prince Harry.

Multiple royal experts echoed the sentiment to Fox News Digital after royal author Robert Jobson told Page Six that Prince William and his estranged brother have "different agendas" and maintain very different relationships with their father.
Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace and Kensington Palace for comment.
KING CHARLES KEPT PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON IN THE DARK ABOUT SECRET HARRY AND MEGHAN REUNION: REPORT

The Sun reported that Prince Harry is expected to visit the U.K. in September and his father, King Charles (center), will offer his son a room at Buckingham Palace in London. (Aaron Chown - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"When it comes to Harry, William drew a line in the sand after the publication of Harry's memoir, 'Spare,' and he is disappointed that his father is not standing up for him," Christopher Andersen, author of "The King," told Fox News Digital.

"William loves his father and appreciates better than anyone how underestimated Charles has been over the years. He wants the king to leave his mark on history. But deep down, he knows he and his family — particularly his wife, Kate — are the future of the monarchy."
WATCH: PRINCE WILLIAM UNLIKELY TO RECONCILE WITH PRINCE HARRY SOON: EXPERT
While Charles and William are described as being "perfectly civil to each other," sources told Page Six there are ongoing disagreements about how the monarchy should be led.
"The problem with William is that he thinks he knows best," royal biographer Hugo Vickers told the outlet.
Prince William, Prince of Wales, meets young people and volunteers in the Common Room at Eagle House on July 9, 2026, in Hastings, England. (WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"King Charles is tired," Andersen stressed to Fox News Digital. "He would like to have everything as it was before Megxit. But he knows how willful William is. Queen Elizabeth's cousin Margaret Rhodes told me more than once that the relationship between Charles and his late mother wasn't cozy. But what people don't know is that the royal family isn't set up to be 'cozy.' Well, it still isn't. It's 'The Firm,' remember?"

Prince William, Prince of Wales and King Charles III walk behind Queen Elizabeth II's coffin as it is transported on a gun carriage from Buckingham Palace to Westminster Hall ahead of her lying in state on Sept. 14, 2022, in London. William is heir to the British throne. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

People magazine reported Harry is expected to visit his home country again in September. The Sun also reported that the king plans to offer him a room at Buckingham Palace in London for his stay. Buckingham Palace and Harry's representatives had no comment on the report when reached by People magazine.

Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital that Charles' reported offer to accommodate Harry in September is "a potential lifeline" that also sends a message of "defiance" to William, who reportedly wants "no further contact with his estranged brother."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex departs from The Invictus Games Foundation Conversation: From Policy to Practice at Chatham House on July 7, 2026, in London. Multiple royal experts told Fox News Digital that there's no doubt King Charles' younger son misses his life in the U.K. (Eamonn M. McCormack/Getty Images)
British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that William is known for being stubborn behind palace doors and is not one to forgive easily.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Prince William (pictured here) did not meet with his estranged younger brother, Prince Harry, who spent time with their father, King Charles III, at Highgrove House, the monarch's private residence, on July 10, 2026. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
"Megxit forced William to grow up fast as the future king," she said.

"Prince Harry’s potential lifeline return to the United Kingdom in September and being offered accommodation at Buckingham Palace by King Charles is, to me, a major sign of defiance to William’s wishes of no future contact with his erstwhile brother," royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"He had to protect the institution while his brother walked away. William believes the monarchy must be seen to do the right thing, even when it's painful. From what I understand, he felt his father didn't handle that firmly enough. He also believes in protecting it by drawing hard lines. But he's not the king yet."

Prince William, Prince of Wales, known as the Duke of Rothesay and Catherine, Princess of Wales, known as the Duchess of Rothesay when in Scotland, smile to well-wishers as they arrive for a visit to Aros Hall, a local community hub on April 29, 2025, in Tobermory, Scotland. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"Where Charles may want to smooth things over, to play peacemaker with Harry, William and Catherine are determined to set boundaries. Charles is reigning, but William and Catherine are planning. And that planning is starting to look a lot like leading. Charles wants healing. William and Catherine want survival and stability. William is not doing this to be difficult. He’s doing it because he believes it’s right."

Since marrying in 2018 and making their royal exit in 2020, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex have been attempting to carve out their own independent roles outside the monarchy. (Joshua Sammer/Getty Images)

Royal experts told Fox News Digital that William and Harry have remained estranged since the Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as senior working royals in 2020 and relocated to California. Harry and Meghan have maintained that relentless tabloid scrutiny and what they describe as a lack of support from the palace drove their decision to leave royal life.

Prince William, Prince of Wales and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex attend the Committal Service for Queen Elizabeth II at St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle on Sept. 19, 2022, in Windsor, England. (Getty Images)

Since stepping away from royal life, Harry and Meghan have publicly aired their grievances in high-profile interviews and documentaries. Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," further deepened the fallout within the royal family.
Prince Harry's book "Spare" is displayed in a bookstore on Dec. 16, 2023, in Bath, England. (Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

On July 10, the king hosted his younger son and his family for the first time in years in what royal observers viewed as an effort to repair the longstanding rift. The Sussexes secretly met with the king and Queen Camilla at Highgrove House, a country estate west of London, Buckingham Palace confirmed.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, relocated to California in 2020. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

Vanity Fair royal correspondent Katie Nicholl reported that, according to sources, "not even the Prince and Princess of Wales were made aware that the meeting was taking place." A source close to Charles also told Nicholl the hour-long meeting was "completely cloak-and-dagger, orchestrated by the king."
Meanwhile, William and Kate attended the DMI Royal Charity Polo Cup 2026 at Guards Polo Club in Windsor. The brothers did not see each other.
Kate Middleton kisses Prince William as she presents the prizes after the DMI Royal Charity Polo Cup 2026. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Obviously, King Charles and Prince William are very different characters, sometimes with conflicting temperaments," royal expert Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "What no one can alter is that William, Kate, and their family are the future of the monarchy. And it is natural for the king, who is battling cancer, to want to see his grandchildren."
British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital there's no feud between Prince William and his father, King Charles. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Fitzwilliams argued that William made his disapproval clear on the day the king and queen saw the Sussexes by being absent from the reunion.
"William is making it clear that he has his own set of principles, his own set of rules about what is right and wrong," Andersen said.
A general view of Buckingham Palace in London, England, on July 6, 2026. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

"He feels Harry has violated those rules one too many times. It's not entirely personal. William has a strong sense of duty when it comes not only to his family but also to his country and his family's place in history. He feels Harry has shot the royal family's reputation full of holes. And for what? To become a SoCal influencer?"
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

Prince Harry (left) and Prince William (right) attend the unveiling of a statue of their mother, Princess Diana, at The Sunken Garden in Kensington Palace, London on July 1, 2021, which would have been her 60th birthday. Royal experts told Fox News Digital the last time the brothers spoke was in 2022 during Queen Elizabeth II's funeral. (Dominic Lipinski/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
"William feels Harry has betrayed not only the current generation of royals but also past generations, including their grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, and future generations," Andersen added.

British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that while reports of a fracture between Charles and William are overstated, the two are far from aligned on how to deal with Harry. Whether father and son can find common ground on Harry remains to be seen.

From left: Prince William, Prince of Wales, King Charles III and Queen Camilla attend the Thistle Service at St. Giles' Cathedral in Edinburgh, Scotland on July 1, 2026. (Aaron Chown/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
"Prince William is no fool," Fordwich said. "Every time his zero-tolerance approach is proven correct, his influence increases."
Prince Harry attends the Time100 Sports Gala at Pier Sixty on July 16, 2026, in New York City. (WWD via Getty Images)
In May 2025, Harry told the BBC he would like to reconcile with his family.
"There's no point in continuing to fight anymore."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Anthony Fauci's Hollywood supporters: Julia Roberts, Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom among celebrity backers
summary: From Julia Roberts' "personal hero" to Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom's "Fauci Gang," Hollywood's biggest stars rallied behind Dr. Anthony Fauci during COVID-19.
story: Laura Ingraham and Raymond Arroyo examine newly released diary entries from Dr. Anthony Fauci, highlighting his fascination with Hollywood and celebrity culture. The entries detail Fauci's interactions with celebrities like Julia Roberts and Barbra Streisand.
Julia Roberts, Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom were among Dr. Anthony Fauci's biggest celebrity supporters during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.

As the 85-year-old infectious disease expert became the face of America's COVID-19 response after the pandemic became a global crisis in March 2020, he also attracted an unlikely fan club in Hollywood – including Brad Pitt portraying him on "Saturday Night Live at Home."

While chronicling his management of the spiraling health emergency, Fauci also wrote frequently of his rapidly rising fame in his private 2020 journals, which were released by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky, earlier this week.
FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

TOM HANKS JOKES ABOUT THE NAME HE WOULD GIVE CORONAVIRUS VACCINE

title: American Red Cross declares national blood crisis as type O supply drops to dangerous levels
summary: The American Red Cross declared a blood crisis across the nation as donations hit a four-year summer low, forcing limits on type O blood distributions to hospitals.
story: The American Red Cross declares a critical national blood shortage crisis as supply levels hit dangerously low levels across the United States. Dr. Baia Lasky, medical director for the organization, joins 'Fox & Friends First' to explain the severe impact on hospitals, detail the urgent need for type O donations, and guide viewers on how to help.
The American Red Cross has declared a "blood crisis" across the nation.
The organization released a warning about the second-ever blood supply crisis this week after blood donations fell to a four-year summer low.
This decline worsens an emergency shortage that "threatens the availability of lifesaving blood for patients across the country," the organization wrote in a press release.
MICROPLASTICS DETECTED IN MOST HEART ATTACK PATIENTS' BLOOD IN STARTLING NEW STUDY

The Red Cross is now limiting distributions of type O blood to hospitals, as the nation’s largest single provider of blood products now has less than a one-day national supply of type O positive blood.
Type O blood accounts for about 60% of Red Cross blood distributions and is essential for both everyday patient care and medical emergencies.
A volunteer is pictured donating blood during an American Red Cross blood drive at Hollywood's Magic Castle in Los Angeles, California, July 28, 2026. (Getty Images)
Type O positive is the most commonly transfused blood type, according to the Red Cross, and can be safely given to about 80% of patients.
Type O negative remains the universal blood type "relied upon when every second counts."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
While thousands of Americans show up to donate blood, these donations are reportedly not keeping up with hospital demand during summer trauma season.

This summer’s conditions, amid extreme heat, poor air quality and foodborne illnesses, have contributed to lower donor turnout, the Red Cross reported. Other blood collectors have also reported critical shortages this summer.
A clinician deposits a blood collection tube during an American Red Cross blood drive at Hollywood's Magic Castle on July 28, 2026, in Los Angeles.  (Getty Images)
The Red Cross advised that just three more donors at each blood drive can end the crisis and stabilize the blood supply.
It encourages Americans to book an appointment by using the Blood Donor App, visiting RedCrossBlood.org, or by calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Chris Hrouda, president of Red Cross Biomedical Services, shared information about the developing emergency in a statement.

"The Red Cross takes its responsibility as the nation’s largest single provider of blood products incredibly seriously and has worked tirelessly to strengthen the blood supply for our hospital partners," he said.
Pedestrians walk past the American Red Cross Blood Donation Center in Boston, Massachusetts, on July 14, 2026. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)
Following the organization’s first national blood crisis in January 2022, Hrouda said the Red Cross has put "additional safeguards" in place to help "prevent a crisis like that from happening again."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"But this summer, blood donations simply are not keeping pace with hospital demand, and inventories — especially type O blood — remain under significant strain," he said.

"Every donation has the potential to help save lives, and we urgently need everyone who is eligible to make an appointment to give blood as soon as possible."

title: Shark Week warnings as experts reveal 6 ways to reduce your risk of a shark bite
summary: White shark activity is ramping up along both coasts this August, and experts share six critical tips to avoid a dangerous shark encounter.
story: A great white shark's powerful breach near a boogie boarder off Newport Beach early Saturday created a heart-pounding scene as onlookers watched the massive animal explode from the water nearby.
Shark sightings are common each summer from coast to coast — and though attacks are rare, they do happen.
In August, shark activity begins to ramp up as they migrate and feed along the way, often bringing different species close to shore, according to experts.

Dr. Chris Lowe, professor of marine biology and director of the Shark Lab at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB), confirmed there has been an increase in white shark activity so far this year.
SHARK SIGHTINGS SPIKE NEAR AMERICA'S BEACHES AS JULY 4 CROWDS HEAD TO SHORE FOR WEEKEND
"We expect by August, September or October to see even more sharks off the Southern California coast," he told Fox News Digital.
Even in waters where sharks are frequently found, human encounters rarely lead to bites, experts say. (iStock)

Wyatt Wernath, national spokesperson for the American Lifeguard Association and a retired ocean rescue chief based in Cocoa Beach, Florida, said they've seen typical numbers for this time of year, although there have been "a couple little nibbles" where people were "bit on the heels or the toes."
For those swimming or surfing in the ocean, the experts shared the following six tips to avoid a dangerous shark encounter.
No. 1: Know before you go
Before visiting a new beach, experts advise locating lifeguards and checking for shark sightings, rip currents, jellyfish and other hazards.
10-FOOT GREAT WHITE SHARK SPOTTED SWIMMING DANGEROUSLY CLOSE TO YOUNG PEOPLE

It's important to recognize and understand the flag systems on the beach that can signal certain conditions, Wernath noted. Red flags typically indicate high hazard, yellow flags mean heed caution and green flags mean low hazard.
Red flags typically indicate high hazard, yellow flags mean heed caution and green flags mean low hazard. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
A purple or blue flag indicates the presence of marine life. Combination red and blue flags signal hazardous marine life, such as a shark or dangerous jellyfish.
"If you can prepare yourself by knowing before you go, you’re going to have a much safer and enjoyable vacation or trip to the open water where the sharks live," Wernath said.
No. 2: Avoid other animal activity
Other suspicious animal activity in the water — such as fish, birds and even seals — could mean a shark is nearby.
"If you see the water percolating on the top, that's the fish running from the predators," Wernath said. "Don't go in the water, get out of the water."
SHARK WEEK SHOCKER AS GREAT WHITE BREACHES JUST YARDS FROM OBLIVIOUS BOOGIE BOARDER
"If you see birds diving into the water, and they're feeding kind of erratically, don't go into the water."
Lowe, who runs the California Shark Beach Safety Program, also recommends avoiding dead marine life that could attract sharks.
Other suspicious animal activity in the water — such as fish, birds and even seals — could mean a shark is nearby. (JOSEPH PREZIOSO/AFP via Getty Images)

"If you're out on your surfboard and a seal climbs on your board, that seal isn't trying to bond with you. It's probably trying to get out of the water because it knows there's a big shark around," he said.
SHARK WEEK PUTS SHARK BITE SURVIVAL IN FOCUS WITH ER DOC'S EXPERT TIPS
Avoid bait balls, which are dense schools of fish targeted by predators, Lowe advised. If one forms beneath your surfboard, move away to avoid an approaching shark.
No. 3: Don't stray too far from shore
While some "toe nibblers" in Florida have been known to attack on the shoreline, deep-water predators pose a risk as well, the experts warned.
"They might occasionally bite a person, but we don't really know why."
California has about three shark bites per year and a fatality about every third year, according to Lowe — but numbers change as the population increases and more people seek out offshore recreation.
"When people start going out into the open ocean ... they may be encountering shark species that haven't been around people before," he said. "And therefore, you're a novelty."
Fishing content creator Henry Gibbs was bitten by a grey reef shark while spearfishing in Fiji. (Getty Images)
Ocean spear fishing and kayak fishing are examples of "risky" excursions that have gained popularity in the last few decades, Lowe noted.

"Not only do you have a bloody fish on the end of your spear, but you're out around sharks that might not have been around people before," he said. "So, we just don't know how those sharks will react."
SHARK WEEK FANS MAY WANT TO THINK TWICE BEFORE EATING THIS OCEAN PREDATOR, EXPERTS WARN
"If you're kayak fishing, and you've got your legs in the water, and you’ve got a bloody fish, your leg could get mistaken by an excited shark trying to steal your fish."
When diving or snorkeling, it’s important not to present yourself "as prey," Wernath warned.
No. 4: Skip dawn and dusk swims; never swim alone
Dawn and dusk are peak feeding times for many sharks, increasing the risk of encounters.
Because sharks can mistake people for prey, Lowe recommends avoiding murky water and shiny jewelry that can mimic fish scales.
Because sharks can mistake people for prey, experts recommend avoiding murky water and shiny jewelry that can mimic fish scales. (iStock)
The chances of being bitten are statistically lower when swimming in a group than alone, Lowe said — and if trouble arises, others are there to help.
No. 5: React quickly
During a close encounter, it's important to confirm that the animal is actually a shark, as dolphin and stingray fins can look similar in the water.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Unlike dolphins and stingrays, which typically show a single fin before disappearing underwater, sharks often reveal both their dorsal and tail fins.
"Tail fins will be moving more in a sweeping motion," Wernath said. "It won't go under gradually like a submarine. It won't arc like a dolphin in a rolling fashion."
In an aerial view, a juvenile white shark swims in the clear, shallow water of the Pacific Ocean off the coast of La Jolla on Nov. 22, 2023, in San Diego, California. (Getty Images)
If a shark is identified, give it space and calmly exit the water.

"Don't splash, don't cause a commotion, which will attract the shark, but just get out," Lowe said. "If you're on a surfboard or a boogie board, try to pull yourself up onto it, and just don't present yourself as prey."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"If you see the shark, always keep your eyes on it," he advised. "Follow it, track it, let the shark know you see it, turn your body toward it."
"If the shark comes closer, you can just slowly back up and keep watching it. If you lose track of it, the first place you should always look is behind you."
Unlike dolphins and stingrays, which typically show a single fin before disappearing underwater, sharks often reveal both their dorsal and tail fins. (iStock)
A shark approaching from behind is usually trying to investigate without being noticed. Once it realizes it has been spotted, however, "most of the time, the gig is up," Lowe said.
If it continues to approach, he recommends giving it "a good bop in the nose" to discourage it from coming closer.
"If the shark gets really close, I'm always an advocate of striking out at them. I think humans need to let sharks know that they're not supposed to get close to us," he added.
No. 6: Respect the species
Experts say the key to safely coexisting with sharks is respecting their habitat and behavior while avoiding actions that could make people appear to be prey.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"They're much more intelligent than we give them credit for," Wernath said, noting that they carefully assess potential prey before attacking. "They’re hunters. They're going to look around and make sure they can get to a prey without getting hurt."
The biggest misconception about sharks is that if they’re nearby, they’re going to bite you, Lowe said, adding that research proves this "simply isn't true."
CSULB Shark Lab researcher Dr. Ryan Logan spear tags a great white shark off Huntington Beach, California, on Sunday, March 9, 2025. (Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)
Although human and shark populations have grown thanks to conservation efforts, shark bites haven't increased as expected.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"They might occasionally bite a person, but we don't really know why," Lowe went on. "We don't know if they're biting because they mistake us as food ... [or] because they feel we're a threat."

"Based on our last six years of data using drones, we see white sharks around people pretty much every day, and they seem to largely ignore people," he added. "What that clearly tells me is that humans are not on any shark's menu."
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Hiker's unexplained death exposes deadly alcohol withdrawal risk many don't recognize
summary: Alcohol withdrawal seizures can strike 24 to 48 hours after the last drink, turning wilderness settings into life-threatening traps for heavy drinkers.
story: The actor explained that his wife gave him an ultimatum when it came to his drinking, which got him to stop.

When hiker Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, was found dead near Sykes Hot Springs in California’s Ventana Wilderness, initial speculation pointed to foul play, according to a press release from the Monterey County Sheriff's Office.
However, official coroner's reports revealed her cause of death to be probable alcohol withdrawal seizures brought on by chronic alcohol use disorder.
Friends who were hiking with Shields said she had gone to the river that morning. A short time later, one of them found her unresponsive in the water, according to reports.
IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

"This is a probable seizure that occurred as a result of chronic alcohol use disorder, but there was nothing that stood out that indicated any type of criminal activity," Andres Rosas, commander and the primary public information officer for the Monterey County Sheriff's Office, told KSBW 8.
Given the results of the investigation and forensic examination, no further investigation is taking place.
The recent death of a Big Sur hiker was ruled a probable case of fatal alcohol withdrawal seizures, exposing a dangerous and often hidden medical crisis. (iStock)
The incident highlights a little-known danger of severe alcohol dependence, as suddenly stopping alcohol can trigger life-threatening neurological events.

Alcohol acts as a depressant on the central nervous system. When someone drinks heavily over a prolonged period, the brain adapts by ramping up chemical signals to keep bodily systems functioning, according to experts.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
When alcohol is abruptly stopped, that blocker on the central nervous system is removed. The brain then enters a state of dangerous overexcitation, leading to severe hyperarousal.
Withdrawal symptoms typically begin within six to 24 hours after the last drink, with the risk of seizures peaking between 24 and 48 hours.
Alcohol withdrawal can quickly progress from tremors, sweating and anxiety to severe seizures and a condition called delirium tremens. (iStock)
In wilderness settings or isolated locations, a sudden seizure can result in immediate loss of consciousness, trauma, respiratory arrest or an inability to seek emergency care, experts note.
Clinical guidelines from the National Institutes of Health categorize alcohol withdrawal by the following key progression stages.
Stage 1 (6 to 12 hours post-drink)

This may include minor withdrawal symptoms, including insomnia, tremors, anxiety, gastrointestinal upset, headache, diaphoresis (excessive sweating), heart palpitations, anorexia, nausea, tachycardia (abnormally fast resting heart rate) and hypertension.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Stage 2 (12 to 24 hours post-drink)
This stage is marked by visual, auditory or tactile hallucinations.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Stage 3 (24 to 72 hours post-drink)

People in this stage may experience sudden loss of consciousness accompanied by severe muscle contractions (seizures). Another potential symptom is delirium tremens, a medical emergency involving extreme agitation, fever, racing heart, hyperthermia and cardiac instability.
Attempting to detox without medical supervision can result in sudden loss of consciousness, trauma and death, experts warn. (iStock)

Health agencies, including the National Institutes of Health, strongly advise that individuals with a history of heavy drinking or prior withdrawal episodes never attempt to detox alone or in remote settings.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Medical detox programs use tailored medication protocols to safely taper brain activity and prevent seizures.

Help is available for people struggling with alcohol use disorder. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration National Helpline provides free, confidential treatment referrals 24 hours a day at 1-800-662-4357.
