title: Smithsonian America 250 exhibit features 3x more liberal items than conservative ones
summary: The Smithsonian's America 250th anniversary exhibit features nearly two dozen items for liberal causes but just seven representing conservatism.
story: Heritage expert Mike Gonzalez called out the Smithsonian National Museum of American History for the

A Smithsonian exhibit designed to commemorate America’s 250th birthday displays numerous objects linked to key points in the nation’s history, though it provides relatively little representation of Christianity or conservatism despite ample coverage for LGBT rights and racial justice movements, among other liberal causes, a Fox News Digital review of the exhibit's online catalog found.

In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness is an exhibit curated by the Smithsonian Institution with the aim of displaying 250 objects that help to tell the story of America from the 1700s to the present. Among these objects are historically significant items, such as a compass from the 1806 Lewis and Clark expedition, a dress belonging to Dolly Madison, Abraham Lincoln’s hat and the desk the Declaration of Independence was written on.

Also included in the exhibit, according to an online catalog published by the Smithsonian, are a number of objects with clear ties to modern liberal politics, such as a pink "p-ssy hat" worn by a participant of the 2017 Women's March, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s gavel, monarch butterfly wings worn by an illegal immigrant activist and a typewriter belonging to liberal writer Maya Angelou.
Next to Angelou’s typewriter is a picture of a 1970s drag queen "wearing an off-the-shoulder shimmery gown," according to a visual description of the exhibit published by the Smithsonian.
TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

Women, wearing the so-called Pussy Hat, pose for a selfie during a rally to mark the International Women's Day in Copenhagen, Denmark on March 8, 2017.  (Nikolai Linares/Scanpix Denmark/AFP via Getty Images))
The exhibit’s selections are drawing scrutiny as President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans challenge the Smithsonian’s portrayal of American history around the nation’s 250th anniversary.

Fox News Digital reviewed the Smithsonian’s online catalog and grouped objects according to the movements, causes and institutions identified in the museum’s descriptions, finding seven tied to conservative movements, compared with nearly two dozen tied to causes including LGBT rights, abortion access, racial justice, organized labor and Democratic politics.
The apparent domination of liberal causes in an exhibit designed to celebrate the contributions of all Americans to the nation's history could further inflame conservative criticisms of the museum.
While the exhibit examines how left-of-center individuals and movements shaped American history, conservatives have less representation.

Just seven items representing conservative movements — a MAGA hat, a Tea Party placard, a pro-life sign, a dress worn by Melania Trump, a sign opposing the feminist-backed Equal Rights Amendment, a Ronald Reagan campaign T-shirt and a National Rifle Association button — are presented by the Smithsonian, according to its online catalog.

By comparison, the same catalog shows that liberal causes — such as LGBT rights, farm-worker rights, abortion access, racial justice, environmentalism, labor unions and the Democratic Party — collectively have nearly two dozen items representing them.
THE WAR ON AMERICA’S JUDEO-CHRISTIAN ROOTS THREATENS EVERYTHING WE SHARE
The sweeping review first includes eight museums, most of which are under the Smithsonian Institution. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
Among those, the Smithsonian chose four total items representing the gay rights movement, for example.

That wasn't far behind the six it curated to represent Christianity, including items from churches and a Bible, per its catalog. Christianity historically was America's dominant faith, influencing nearly all aspects of life, though it has declined in prominence in recent decades.
Even the items representing Christianity, however, include undertones of racial justice.

A pew from a Black Presbyterian church, for example, is accompanied by a description of its pastor's racial activism. The one Bible on display as part of the exhibit, meanwhile, discusses the owner's anti-slavery sentiments.

Other religions, such as Judaism, with a Seder plate and a Hanukkah lamp, and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day saints, colloquially known as Mormons, with a plate depicting one of their temples, received representation as well.

Among the LGBT artifacts displayed by the Smithsonian is a red tie that belonged to the late lesbian activist Carmen Vázquez. A description for the item notes that she described it as her "seduction necktie."

"Vázquez was born in Puerto Rico and grew up in New York City. After College, she lived in San Francisco for many years, honing her political understanding of immigrant rights and women’s and public health," the online exhibit description continues. "Her endless energy for LGBTQ+ rights and justice for all, and her work, writing, and speeches ensured the safety and capacity to thrive of countless people across the United States."
LGBTQ PRESS CONFERENCE AT TRACK MEET INVOLVING TRANS ATHLETE DESCENDS INTO CHAOS, POLICE SUMMONED

A photograph of President Donald Trump and a short plaque next to it are on display at the Smithsonian's National Portrait Gallery's "American Presidents" exhibit on Sunday, Jan. 11, 2026 in Washington. (Anna Johnson/The Associated Press )

The online catalog also shows that nearly two-dozen items displayed at the exhibit are related to recent waves of Asian and Latino immigration. Earlier migrant groups such as the Irish, French and Italians, received just one entry each.

One display dedicated to recent immigrants is a soccer ball donated by the founder of the Fugees soccer team for refugee children in Clarkston, Georgia, describing how the group "overcame anti-immigrant backlash."

The Smithsonian did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital. However, comments made by the National Museum of American History's director provide some insight as to why curators made the decisions they did when selecting items for the exhibit.

"How do you structure a commemoration, celebration and time for reflection?" Anthea Hartig, the museum’s director, told British newspaper The Guardian. "What we landed on were those moments where individuals or communities had fought for recognition and advocated for their own sense of identity and self in their role in creating and becoming a part of the United States. But we also wanted to do the playful."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Beyond items of political or ideological significance, the exhibit also makes an effort to showcase historical changes to domestic life, technology and pop culture through the display of everyday objects.

Various household appliances from different points in American history, props from the Star Wars movies, currency spanning hundreds of years, instruments belonging to famous musicians, technological advancements in areas such as video games and telecommunications and sports paraphernalia, like hockey gloves worn during the 1980 "miracle on ice" Olympic match against the Soviet Union, are all on display.

title: Liberal court stuns with ruling that hands Trump major immigration win
summary: A liberal-leaning First Circuit panel reversed two district court orders blocking Trump's TPS termination for South Sudan and Ethiopia migrants.
story: DHS Chief Counsel James Percival said a group of federal district judges—not the judiciary as a whole—are repeatedly blocking deportations and Temporary Protected Status rollbacks despite SCOTUS rulings, calling it "naked political activism."

A liberal-led federal appeals court handed President Donald Trump two immigration victories Wednesday, reversing separate district court orders that had delayed the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for migrants from South Sudan and Ethiopia.

The judgments from the First Circuit Court of Appeals come after U.S. District Judges Brian Murphy and Patti Saris issued back-to-back orders temporarily blocking the Trump administration's termination of TPS for Ethiopia and South Sudan, respectively, late last week. The rulings drew sharp criticism from legal experts and Trump administration officials, who called the judges "rogue" and argued their decisions defied the Supreme Court.
The three-judge First Circuit panel consisted of Judges Julie Rikelman and Seth Aframe, both appointed by President Joe Biden, and Judge Joshua Dunlap, who was appointed by President Donald Trump.
BIDEN JUDGE BLOCKING ETHIOPIAN DEPORTATIONS DESPITE SCOTUS RULING CLASHED WITH ICE BEFORE
President Donald Trump during an announcement in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, D.C., on July 29, 2026. (Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
SUPREME COURT WEIGHS TRUMP EFFORT TO TERMINATE TEMPORARY PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIAN, SYRIAN MIGRANTS

In nearly identical rulings, the majority liberal panel found that the lower court judges' orders conflicted with the Supreme Court's decision in Mullin v. Doe, which held that courts cannot block TPS terminations based on non-constitutional claims.

"Mullin held that 'the TPS statute's judicial-review bar applies to all non-constitutional claims' challenging the Secretary of Homeland Security's determination with respect to the termination of a TPS designation," the judges wrote.
Iowa Solicitor General Eric Wessan told Fox News Digital that the First Circuit correctly applied the precedent established by the Supreme Court.

"These are clear wins for President Trump following his big win at the U.S. Supreme Court, explaining that district courts are not supposed to second guess TPS terminations, and even as this plays out, we're moving towards the end of this litigation because district courts should not be hearing these disputes, and that's what the Supreme Court said," Wessan told Fox News Digital.

U.S. President Donald Trump takes questions from the media during a bilateral meeting with President of Lebanon Joseph Aoun in the Oval Office of the White House on July 21, 2026, in Washington, D.C. U.S. District Court Judge Patti Saris attends the opening ceremony for the Justice Stephen G. Breyer Community Learning Center on Courts and the Constitution at the federal courthouse in Boston, Massachusetts, March 25, 2025. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images; Brian Snyder/Reuters)
SUPREME COURT'S LATEST IMMIGRATION RULING WILL CAUSE AMERICANS TO 'DIE AND SUFFER' ATTORNEY WARNS
A Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson welcomed the rulings as "a win for the rule of law and common sense."

"Temporary Protected Status is exactly that—temporary," the spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "For too long, TPS has been allowed to function as a de facto amnesty program despite Congress never intending it to be permanent."

The lawsuits were brought by African Communities Together, a New York-based immigrant advocacy organization that serves as the lead plaintiff in both cases, alongside individual TPS recipients from Ethiopia and South Sudan. The plaintiffs argue DHS unlawfully ended the protections in violation of the Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution, alleging the agency failed to properly assess conditions in the two countries and that the decisions were motivated by racial discrimination.

Murphy and Saris temporarily blocked the Trump administration from terminating TPS last week, issuing procedural orders to preserve the status quo while they considered whether the plaintiffs should be permitted to amend their complaints to pursue renewed constitutional claims.
DHS EVISCERATES MEDIA FOR ‘ABSOLUTE ABSURDITY’ OVER CONCERN ABOUT ‘WORST OF THE WORST’ ACTIVIST JUDGES LIST

While the Supreme Court's decision in Mullin v. Doe foreclosed most statutory challenges to TPS terminations, it left open the possibility that courts could consider claims alleging constitutional violations.

U.S. District Judge Brian Murphy temporarily blocked key Trump administration decisions to terminate Temporary Protected Status. (United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary/ REUTERS/Nathan Howard)
However, Wessan said the district judges were operating outside the "legal bounds" by blocking the TPS terminations before any constitutional claims had been established.
"If they want to let the plaintiffs amend their complaint, they're allowed to do that, but in the meantime, TPS is over," Wessan told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The First Circuit's decisions mark the latest setback for Murphy and Saris after the Trump administration accused both judges of effectively sidestepping the Supreme Court's June ruling. After Murphy's order, DHS General Counsel James Percival wrote on X that the district judge was engaged in "mutiny against the Supreme Court," while he described Saris' ruling as "open defiance" of the justices' decision.
Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of Murphy and Saris for comment.
Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

title: Investigators believe Iranian hackers are likely behind cyberattack on Minnesota water systems: report
summary: More than 30 Minnesota water systems were hit by a coordinated cyberattack that officials say was likely orchestrated by Iranian hackers, a report said.
story: Retired Navy SEAL Mike Sarraille discusses the expanding U.S.-Iran conflict after a reported cyberattacks on Minnesota water systems and military strikes, stressing the crucial importance of securing global shipping lanes.
U.S. investigators believe a cyberattack that targeted dozens of water systems in Minnesota this week likely was orchestrated by Iranian hackers, a report said.

Minnesota IT Services (MNIT) said the "coordinated cyberattack targeted operational technology at more than 30 Minnesota community water systems" on Sunday and Monday, but the Minnesota Department of Health is "not aware of any active requests from Minnesota cities to have their residents modify their drinking water usage."
U.S. and state officials and others familiar with the incident told The New York Times that Iranian hackers were likely behind the cyberattack.

The newspaper reported that three state officials briefed on an investigation into the cyberattack said the tradecraft used and the absence of a ransom demand led analysts to initially determine Iran was involved. Officials also cautioned that the assessment could change as more data is collected by investigators, according to the newspaper.
However, President Donald Trump said during a Cabinet meeting Friday that he would "blame it on Minnesota and the governor."

"Today, I just want to mention that, we heard in Minnesota there was a cyberattack, and they blame it on Iran. I don't think so. I think I blame it on Minnesota because they're grossly incompetent. There was a cyberattack of 30 water plants, and I would blame it on Minnesota and the governor, the corrupt governor of Minnesota," Trump said, referencing Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, a Democrat. "They like to say, 'oh it's Iran.' Iran should be so lucky. Iran's got bigger problems than worrying about Minnesota."
IRAN-LINKED HACKERS TARGET US MEDICAL TECH COMPANY

A water tower is seen Thursday, July 30, 2026, in Plymouth, Minn. A cyberattack targeted operating technology at more than 30 water systems in Minnesota, including Plymouth's, earlier this week, state officials said. (Ellen Schmidt/AP)
The FBI said earlier in a statement to Fox News Digital on Friday that it is "aware of recent public reporting around Water and Wastewater sectors."
"The FBI and our interagency partners are fully engaged to protect critical infrastructure and we remain well-equipped to protect against cyber threats of all varieties," the FBI added.
The New York Times reported that the hackers targeted infrastructure used to manage and monitor water towers operated by municipal governments.
The mayor of the city of Braham, Nate George, said on Monday, a "plant operator found that the water tower was calling for water, but the well was not operating."

"After learning that similar problems were occurring in at least four other Minnesota communities, Braham staff determined that the plant’s computerized control system had been compromised," he continued.

"Public works isolated the affected system, restored a backup, and restarted the plant within approximately 90 minutes. While the plant was offline, residents continued receiving water from the city’s water tower. City administration temporarily requested that residents conserve water to prevent the tower’s limited supply from being exhausted," George added.
LIVE UPDATES ON IRAN WAR: TRUMP ANNOUNCES HAMAS DISARMAMENT DEAL WHILE SAUDI ARABIA LAUNCHES RED SEA DEFENSE COALITION

A woman is seen holding an Iranian flag during a religious ceremony during Eid al-Adha on May 26, 2026, in Qom, Iran. Iran is believed to be behind recent cyberattacks in Minnesota, a report said. (Majid Saeedi/Getty Images)
In a statement shared with Fox News Digital, MNIT noted that "the investigation remains active, and Minnesota has not attributed the activity to a specific actor."

MNIT said it "continues to collaborate with federal, state, local, Tribal, and private-sector partners to investigate the attack, support affected communities, and strengthen the security of Minnesota's critical infrastructure."

"Cyberattacks against critical infrastructure require a coordinated, whole-of-government response," John Israel, MNIT assistant commissioner and Minnesota chief information security officer, said in a statement. "MNIT is working side by side with our partners to share intelligence, support affected communities, and help utilities restore operations safely while strengthening defenses against future attacks."
Israel told the Times that the breach was first detected Sunday and that hackers targeted 36 municipal water systems.
"Minnesota was one of the early detectors of this, but we’re seeing that this same threat activity has likely been occurring in other states throughout the nation," he was quoted as saying.

Nick Andersen, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s (CISA) acting director, told the newspaper that the agency was aware of "multiple potential incidents affecting local water utilities."

In the days leading up to the incident, CISA issued an advisory warning U.S. organizations of "ongoing Iranian-affiliated cyber activity targeting internet-connected operational technology (OT) devices."

"Iranian cyber actors continue to target U.S. critical infrastructure, and the FBI is committed to identifying, disrupting, and imposing costs on those responsible," Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Division said in the advisory.

It stated that a "group of Iranian-affiliated actors" has "targeted devices spanning multiple U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, including Water and Wastewater Systems, Energy and Government Services and Facilities, to include local municipalities."

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) also issued an advisory on Thursday "to warn critical infrastructure asset owners and operators that malicious cyber actors are conducting cyber attacks targeting Operational Technology devices."

title: Ben Sasse's latest pancreatic cancer update comes amid his stark warning about America's future
summary: Ben Sasse says his tumors shrank by over 80% on a clinical trial drug as he battles metastatic pancreatic cancer and warns about China and AI.
story: Former Senator Ben Sasse shares update on his cancer battle and biggest challenges facing America in an interview at the Western Conservative Summit exclusively shared with Fox News Digital. (Credit: Western Conservative Summit)
FIRST ON FOX: Battling Stage 4 pancreatic cancer, former Nebraska Sen. Ben Sasse is looking ahead with optimism for his own health but expressed less hope for America's future.
He cautioned that America's greatest challenges are still to come in a pre-recorded interview for the Western Conservative Summit in Lakewood, Colorado, exclusively shared with Fox News Digital.

"Pancreatic cancer is nasty, and I would never wish it on my worst enemy, but I also would never want to go back to a stage of my life where I didn't know the power of pancreatic cancer prayer," said Sasse, quoting Pastor Tim Keller at Redeemer Presbyterian Church in New York.

Sasse, 54, shared in December 2025 that he has metastatic pancreatic cancer, which has spread to multiple organs — including his liver and lungs. He was initially given three to four months to live but entered a clinical trial for a drug called daraxonrasib, an oral therapy (pill) that is designed to block the defective gene that triggers uncontrolled cellular growth.
PANCREATIC CANCER VACCINE SHOWS PROMISE IN FIRST HUMAN TRIAL, PREVENTING DISEASE IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS
In addition to the daraxonrasi, Sasse credits his faith for helping him beat his original prognosis. (Drew Angerer/Getty Images)

"My tumors have shrunk by over 80% in the six and a half months I've been on this drug," said Sasse in his update. "The drug has been amazing, and I'm grateful for that common grace extension of time."
"We're a couple days away from being seven months since my diagnosis at three to four months to live."

Even as he reflected on his own mortality, Sasse said he's increasingly concerned about the country's future, cautioning that the U.S. must outcompete China, overhaul its failing schools and adapt to an AI-driven economy.

"I want the U.S. Via decentralized corporate structures to rule the world, not CCP, tyrannical, Maoist to rule of the world, and I think most middle powers, most countries in the world, know that somewhere between 25 years from now, we're going to say the world is Western/U.S. led," said Sasse.
CHINA IS BUILDING A MASSIVE SHIP THAT SHOULD SCARE AMERICANS ABOUT THE FUTURE
Ben Sasse sits down at the Western Conservative Summit. (Western Conservative Summit)
He describes a world that is led by the U.S. passing along values with free trade, the rule of law, transparency and acknowledgment of human rights.
The alternative would be "CCP led," said Sasse. "Which is them controlling all trade through Beijing."
From the campus of Colorado Christian University, where conservative leaders gathered for the Western Conservative Summit, Sasse also weighed in on the challenges facing higher education.
"Our educational systems are just a complete disaster," said Sasse.

The latest Nation's Report Card found that roughly one in three eighth graders cannot read at even a basic level, nearly 40% fall below basic in math, and fewer than one-third are proficient in reading, according to the National Assessment Governing Board report for 2025.
BEN SASSE CLAIMS PUBLIC SCHOOLS WERE CREATED TO SEPARATE CATHOLIC KIDS FROM PARENTS, PRIESTS

Sen. Ben Sasse (R-NE) speaks during Attorney General nominee Merrick Garland's confirmation hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee in the Hart Senate Office Building on February 22, 2021, in Washington, D.C. (Al Drago/Getty Images)
Sasse argued that academic benchmarks are too low and that increasing government spending on education has failed to improve student outcomes.
"The potential and the capacity of most souls and most brains is a lot more than that, and we've just got a disastrous system," said Sasse.
Sasse said that the rise of AI is going to "externalize a lot of IQ" changing what schools will teach.

He added that America is entering an AI revolution that will disrupt work, education, and global power.

"A hundred years from now, when we look back on our moment, we're not gonna talk about our politics very much. I think we're gonna talk about the fact that we are living through a technological revolution," said Sasse.

title: House Democrat blasted after early release law freed inmates later charged with murder
summary: Rep. Nellie Pou's COVID-era prison release law freed more than 7,000 inmates early but multiple were later charged with murder, sparking GOP attacks.
story: Jonathan Fahey, former DHS deputy assistant secretary, weighs in on anti-ICE protests in Brooklyn that blocked hospital entrances, condemning NYC Mayor Mamdani's reaction.
A COVID-era prison release law championed by Rep. Nellie Pou, D-N.J., is facing renewed scrutiny after multiple inmates freed early under the program were later charged with murder.
More than 7,000 inmates received an early release starting in November 2020 after then-Gov. Phil Murphy, D-N.J., signed legislation sponsored by Pou, then a New Jersey state senator.

Under the law, state inmates were eligible for early release via "public health emergency credits" if they had less than one year remaining on their sentences and had not been convicted of murder or sexual assault and were not sex offenders.
People serving time for other violent offenses — including aggravated manslaughter and kidnapping — could still receive a shortened sentence of up to eight months.
Rep. Nellie Pou, D-N.J., speaks at a House Homeland Security Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on Feb. 24, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)
NORTH CAROLINA TEACHER'S KILLING REIGNITES SCRUTINY OF ROY COOPER'S CRIMINAL JUSTICE RECORD IN SENATE RACE
Two inmates released under the program later pleaded guilty to or were convicted in separate homicide cases. A third remains in custody awaiting trial on murder and conspiracy charges.

Supporters of the law, including the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), argued the measure was necessary to reduce the prison population amid concerns about overcrowding during the COVID-19 pandemic.
A smaller prison population, according to Pou, would "keep everyone, guards included, safer" from the virus, she wrote in a 2020 statement.
But the New Jersey Democrat has said little publicly about the law since multiple inmates released under the program were linked to grisly killings.
The legislation passed over objections from GOP lawmakers and some county prosecutors, who warned it could endanger public safety by releasing violent offenders early.
Jerry Crawford, 30, was arrested in the shooting death of an 18-year-old just two days after his release on parole supervision in November 2020.
Crawford, who had been serving a burglary sentence, would have otherwise remained incarcerated until the following month, according to the New Jersey Department of Corrections, NJ.com reported.
He is scheduled to stand trial in January 2027 on murder and conspiracy charges, according to New Jersey court records.

Another inmate, 31-year-old Ronny Paden, was released early in November 2020 after the COVID-era program shortened his sentence for aggravated assault and weapons offenses. Two months later, he shot and killed two men at a birthday party.
Paden later pleaded guilty to first-degree aggravated manslaughter and was sentenced to 12 years in state prison.
A third inmate, Theodore Luckey, 47, is serving life without parole after pleading guilty to two counts of first-degree murder.

Rep. Nellie Pou, D-N.J., is facing scrutiny over a COVID-era prison release law she sponsored while serving in the New Jersey Legislature. Jerry Crawford, right, was charged in the killing of an 18-year-old just two days after being released under the program. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images; Cumberland County Jail)
NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'

Luckey attacked and killed an ex-boyfriend with a machete in August 2021, striking him more than 120 times, after being released from prison in May. Prosecutors also said he strangled another man in a hotel room shortly beforehand.

He was released from prison under the program eight months early after completing most of a 15-year prison sentence involving a burglary conviction and illegal possession of a deadly weapon, the New Jersey-based Asbury Park Press reported.
Republicans sharply criticized Pou’s embrace of the early prison release program that freed several repeat offenders.

"Instead of holding criminals accountable, soft-on-crime radical Nellie Pou spearheaded legislation that lets violent offenders off the hook and threatens the safety of law-abiding New Jerseyans," New Jersey Republican Chairwoman Christine Giordano Hanlon told Fox News Digital.
"Nellie is a threat to her constituents’ safety, and they’ll send her packing because of it," National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) spokeswoman Maureen O’Toole said.

A representative for Pou did not directly respond to a request for comment about whether the congresswoman believed the program proved successful, but emphasized Pou’s support for law enforcement and public safety.

"Just this year, Congresswoman Pou voted in favor of more than $253 million in funding to hire and rehire local police and to steer $13.5 million toward state law enforcement agencies to combat drug trafficking," Morghan Cyr, Pou’s campaign manager, said in a statement.

New Jersey Gov.-elect Mikie Sherrill and Gov. Phil Murphy greet the audience before a conversation between Stephen Colbert and Conan O'Brien to benefit Montclair Film at New Jersey Performing Arts Center in Newark, N.J., on Dec. 7, 2025. (Getty Images)
The GOP attacks come as Pou is seeking a second House term in a northern New Jersey House seat that President Donald Trump narrowly carried in 2024.

Pou, a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, has joined House Democratic leadership in voting against GOP-authored legislation ranging from cracking down on illegal immigration to targeting "soft-on-crime" policies in Washington, D.C.
Still, it remains unclear whether Pou will face a serious re-election threat.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report shifted the race in favor of Democrats earlier this year to "Likely Democrat," citing New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill, D-N.J., carrying Pou’s district by nearly 20 points during the 2025 gubernatorial contest.

title: Trump unloads on Cornyn, ties AG nomination fight to bitter Texas primary
summary: Trump accuses Sen. John Cornyn of blocking Todd Blanche's attorney general confirmation over the anti-weaponization fund and audit immunity disputes.
story: President Donald Trump is taking a hardball tactic against Republican rebels demanding concessions for their vote to confirm Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche.
President Donald Trump unleashed more fury on a Senate Republican he worked to oust who is standing in the way of his personal lawyer becoming the next attorney general.
Trump unloaded on Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, over acting Attorney General Todd Blanche’s stalled nomination Friday morning, a day after threatening to withdraw Blanche’s nomination from the Senate.

He accused Cornyn of previously having no issue with the nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund, one of the issues that he and Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., are trying to kill, before Trump endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in their grueling primary showdown.
TRUMP THREATENS TO YANK HIS OWN AG NOMINEE AS GOP REVOLT GROWS
Trump accused Cornyn of backing the nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund before Trump endorsed Paxton. (Jabin Botsford/The Washington Post via Getty Images; Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"John Cornyn never had a problem with the so-called ‘Fund,’ which will not benefit me, but rather the great American Patriots who were hunted down like dogs and whose lives were unfairly and illegally destroyed by the Crooked Joe Biden Administration, until after I decided to Endorse and Support his Republican Primary opponent in Texas, who easily won the Nomination for the United States Senate," Trump said on Truth Social.
Fox News Digital did not immediately receive comment from Cornyn’s office in response to Trump’s remarks.

Cornyn and Tillis are both pushing the Department of Justice (DOJ) and administration to provide explicit, written proposals to permanently nix and rewrite the anti-weaponization fund and Trump’s audit immunity, respectively, that were borne from his settlement deal with the IRS, which Blanche rolled out earlier this year.
DOJ BARS IRS FROM AUDITING TRUMP’S PRIOR TAX RETURNS IN SETTLEMENT ORDER SIGNED BY BLANCHE

The Texas Republican, in particular, wants changes to Trump’s audit immunity spelled out in the deal, and has so far not had his demands met as paper continues to flow back and forth between the lawmakers and administration.
But the lawmakers contend that there’s a force above Blanche that is thwarting the process and further slowing down his confirmation.

"I thought we were pretty close to landing the plane last night, but this morning there's been some more complications," Cornyn told reporters on Thursday. "I think if this were just between me and Todd Blanche, we would have worked this out. But apparently he's getting some pushback from higher-ups at the White House. I don't know who, but this doesn't need to be this hard."
WATCH: GOP HOLDOUT REJECTS TRUMP THREAT AS AG NOMINEE STANDOFF EXPLODES
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche gets sworn in at his confirmation hearing in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee on Capitol Hill. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

Trump appeared unwilling to part with the fund, which has been condemned by Republicans and Democrats over concerns that it would dole out taxpayer dollars to rioters who stormed the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.

"I will always feel that these victims of government abuse should be paid back for what they were forced to endure, their lives have been ruined," Trump said. "Millions of people agree with me, as was proven in my landslide Presidential win, where this was a major subject of debate, and so did John Cornyn, until he lost his Election to an opponent that I Endorsed. Todd Blanche, a good man, should be immediately approved as U.S. Attorney General."
Both Cornyn and Tillis met with Blanche toward the end of the day Thursday to continue hashing out a path forward.

Meanwhile, Trump threatened to yank Blanche’s nomination from the Senate over the impasse after Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, postponed his confirmation hearing scheduled for Thursday.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

His plan would be to wait until both Cornyn and Tillis are out of office next year. But, there’s no guarantee that the Senate would be more welcoming to Blanche after the midterm elections this November.

And Tillis and Cornyn aren’t the only Republicans with reservations about Blanche — Sens. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, and John Curtis, R-Utah, are both on the fence on whether to support him on a full floor vote in the Senate.
Given universal Democratic opposition, their resistance could sink his chances.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Firebrand rep unloads on socialist prime minister as 'hordes of military aged men' swarm European country
summary: Viral video shows tens of thousands of migrants storming Spain's Ceuta enclave from Morocco as Rep. Brandon Gill blames Pedro Sánchez's amnesty program.
story: Thousands of migrants from Morocco pored over the country's border with Spain and into Spain's African enclave of Ceuta on July 30, 2026. (Reuters)

As shocking videos circulate of migrants pouring over the collapsed border of the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, took a swipe at the country’s socialist prime minister, saying, "That's what happens every single time a politician offers amnesty."

Ceuta, a Spanish territory on the tip of Africa, formally requested a national emergency declaration on Thursday after about 60,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco. Video shows hordes of men smiling and posing for cameras, some carrying swimming flippers, and sprinting through the streets as authorities struggle to corral the unruly masses. Other footage shows crowds of migrants emerging from the sea, climbing up onto Ceuta's rocky shores and working their way around border fences.
Gill, a young Republican known for his viral takedowns during congressional hearings, blamed the breakdown on Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who leads the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party.

"Spain's socialist Prime Minister announced he would be giving amnesty to millions of illegal aliens. Now, his country is being invaded by hordes of military aged men from Africa," Gill posted on X. "Because that's what happens every single time a politician offers amnesty."
WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO ‘ABOLISH POLICE’

Rep. Brandon Gill (left), R-Texas, is blaming Spanish socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez for the ongoing border crisis in the Spanish territory of Ceuta, saying, "That's what happens every single time a politician offers amnesty." (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images; Reuters)

Sánchez's socialist government launched an "extraordinary regularization" program earlier this year that allows eligible undocumented migrants already living in Spain to obtain legal residence and work authorization. The government says the policy promotes economic integration, while critics describe it as a mass amnesty.

Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas formally requested that Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declare a national emergency to help respond to the border crisis, Spanish media outlets reported. Madrid, however, denied the request.

Vivas said on Friday that an estimated 60,000 migrants had crossed from Morocco amid the crisis, with most arriving during a massive surge that began Thursday. Spain’s Interior Ministry put the number closer to 50,000.

Spain's Ministry of the Interior said in a statement, according to Spanish outlet El Pais, that "the declaration of a national emergency is part of the state civil protection regulations, which do not consider migratory flows as a risk to the National Civil Protection System, nor do they establish special plans, basic guidelines, or specific civil protection instruments for their management. Therefore, it is not possible to activate this mechanism, as requested by the president of the Government of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas."

Ceuta’s government initially reported that up to 2,000 migrants had crossed during a 10-day period. But the crisis escalated dramatically Thursday, with local officials later raising the estimated number of arrivals to 60,000.
EU ADMITS IT ‘DIDN’T HAVE CONTROL’ ON MIGRATION AS BLOC RUSHES CRACKDOWN AHEAD OF NEW RULES

Migrants run and cheer as they cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco, after swimming over from the Moroccan side and overwhelming police at the city's breakwater, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, in Ceuta, Spain, July 30, 2026. (FARO TV via Reuters)

"The Government of Spain is fully committed to providing an immediate response to the situation in Ceuta. We are mobilizing all necessary resources, working with Moroccan and international authorities, and preparing the necessary measures to restore normalcy as soon as possible," Sánchez wrote in a Thursday post on X.

Back in the U.S., the White House has also criticized Sánchez for the collapse, saying in a statement that "President Trump has long warned Europe what would happen if they continue to implement far-left, globalist policies – including enabling mass migration."
"Spain and other countries who have adopted this destructive philosophy should immediately reverse course or risk their own demise," said the White House.
TRUMP CRITICIZES SPAIN AMID IRAN, NATO RIFT AS PM SANCHEZ FACES QUESTIONS OVER POLITICAL MOTIVES

Migrants cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco by attempting to swim, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, near the border with Ceuta, in Fnideq, Morocco, on July 30, 2026. (Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Sánchez, however, has previously claimed that accepting migrants is necessary to keep Spain's economy alive, arguing the country's low birth rates necessitate accepting immigrants.

"The West needs people. Currently, few of its countries have a rising population growth rate. Unless they embrace migration, they will experience a sharp demographic decline that will prevent them from keeping their economies and public services afloat. Their gross domestic product will stagnate. Their public healthcare and pension systems will suffer. Neither AI nor robots will be able to prevent this outcome... The only option to avoid decline is to integrate migrants in the most orderly and effective way possible," Sánchez wrote in a February op-ed in The New York Times.
Fox News Digital's Robert McGreevy contributed to this report.

title: Foreign robot ban targets China over security fears
summary: The FCC added foreign-produced humanoid robots and connected power inverters to its Covered List, blocking new models from receiving U.S. authorization.
story: Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, introduces the bipartisan Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, aiming to effectively block Chinese-made electric vehicles from the U.S. market. Moreno warns against these vehicles, saying they could potentially allow remote control and pose significant national security threats. He emphasizes protecting the American auto industry and workers from subsidized Chinese exports.

A humanoid robot can carry equipment through a factory or help researchers test new artificial intelligence. However, its cameras can watch everything nearby. Its internet connection can also send valuable information beyond the building. The Trump administration now sees that combination as a potential national security problem.

On July 28, the Federal Communications Commission added foreign-produced advanced robots and connected power inverters to its Covered List. The action blocks many new models from receiving the FCC authorization required before companies can import or sell them in the United States.

Although the final language applies broadly to foreign-produced equipment, China reportedly sits at the center of the crackdown. Officials want to prevent surveillance and cyberattacks while reducing America's reliance on Chinese technology. They also hope companies will move more manufacturing to the United States.
HUMANOID ROBOT VIDEOS SHOW MACHINES LASHING OUT
CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

The FCC is blocking new foreign-made advanced robots and connected power inverters over cybersecurity and national security concerns. (Tang Yanjun/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images)
Why the foreign robot ban is happening now

Humanoid robots are no longer limited to flashy demonstrations that rack up views online. Companies are preparing them for factories and warehouses. Researchers are also testing them inside laboratories. Four-legged robots can inspect dangerous areas or patrol large properties. Meanwhile, robot developers are building new safety systems as these machines begin working closer to people.

That sounds useful, but these machines also see and hear a lot. Many come equipped with cameras and microphones. Other sensors help them map rooms, recognize objects and respond to people. The robot may connect to cloud services for AI processing. A company might also use that connection to install software updates or provide remote support. That connection is where the FCC sees a potential problem.

If a hacker gets inside the system, the robot could collect sensitive information or send data somewhere it should not go. An attacker might also interfere with its movements. In some cases, that person could gain remote control. We have already seen how those risks can surface in ordinary connected machines. A recent security report involving Yarbo robot mowers raised concerns about remote access, live camera feeds and saved Wi-Fi information.

Now think about a more powerful robot working inside a factory or research lab. Federal national security agencies say some foreign-made robots could create unacceptable cybersecurity and supply chain risks. They worry that hostile governments could use the technology to monitor Americans. The machines could also gather intelligence from sensitive locations. A stolen password is bad enough. A hacked robot can move through a building while recording what it sees. It may also operate close to valuable equipment.
How the FCC foreign robot ban works

The FCC did not tell Americans to surrender robots they already own. The government also did not automatically order retailers to remove every foreign robot from store shelves. Instead, the agency added foreign-produced advanced robotic devices to its Covered List.

Equipment on that list generally cannot receive a new FCC authorization. Most connected electronic products need that approval before companies can import, market or sell them in the United States. As a result, the restrictions mainly affect new models that have not received authorization. Previously approved products can remain available, although the FCC reportedly retains the authority to revoke earlier approvals.

Companies may also seek conditional approval. Federal national security agencies can review a device and decide whether it presents an acceptable level of risk. Officials expect many non-Chinese suppliers to reportedly receive exemptions. That suggests the broader foreign-made restriction will hit Chinese manufacturers the hardest.

This move did not come out of nowhere. Lawmakers had already introduced a bipartisan proposal that would block federal agencies from using certain robots tied to foreign adversaries. The latest FCC action reaches much further because it can prevent new products from entering the broader American market.
Why power inverters are included in the crackdown

Power inverters rarely attract the same attention as walking robots. Still, they play an important role in America's energy system. An inverter converts direct current electricity into alternating current electricity. Solar panels and batteries generate or store direct current. Homes, power grids and data centers generally need alternating current.

Many inverters today connect to the internet. Operators use those connections to check performance and install updates. Some systems also allow remote adjustments. However, remote access creates another potential doorway for attackers.

Federal officials worry that foreign companies or hackers could interfere with connected inverters. A coordinated attack might disrupt equipment or expose information about how energy moves through a facility.

A major interruption could affect internet cloud services and the businesses that rely on them. An inverter may look like a metal box mounted beside a solar array. Still, when thousands of connected units feed electricity into important systems, their security becomes much harder to ignore.
OHIO ROBOT COP RETIRES AFTER ZERO ARRESTS
New FCC restrictions could hit Chinese robotics companies hardest while limiting access to lower-cost machines used by U.S. researchers. (REUTERS/Tingshu Wang)
Why China sits at the center of the robot fight

Chinese companies have become major players in advanced robotics. They have gained attention by offering capable machines at prices that U.S. developers may struggle to match. The ban could reportedly hit Unitree especially hard. Counterpoint Research estimates that the Chinese company holds just under one-fifth of the global humanoid robot market.

Unitree has also worked with Nvidia to use its Blackwell AI chips in a robot platform. Nvidia has said data from those robots will remain in the United States. The company also said many Unitree customers in America are universities and research institutions. China strongly criticized the FCC action. Its embassy in Washington accused the United States of unfairly targeting Chinese businesses. It also warned that Beijing could respond if the restrictions harm Chinese interests. Meanwhile, China's Foreign Ministry called the policy protectionist. A spokesperson argued that the restrictions could hurt American companies and consumers. We reached out to Unitree for comment, but did not hear back before our deadline.
Could the robot ban slow American innovation?

The foreign robot ban may give U.S. manufacturers more room to grow. American companies will face less competition from low-cost Chinese machines in the domestic market. However, the policy could create short-term problems for researchers and startups. Some American teams use affordable Chinese robots to test software or train AI systems. Losing access to newer models could raise costs and limit the hardware available for experiments.

The restrictions could also complicate partnerships between U.S. chipmakers and Chinese robotics companies. That may slow certain projects even as Washington tries to strengthen domestic production. The bigger question involves timing. Building a competitive American robotics supply chain will take investment and skilled workers. Manufacturers must also secure motors, sensors and other components. Until that happens, tighter restrictions could leave a gap between the robots American developers want and the machines they can afford.
How to protect yourself when buying a connected robot

You may never bring a humanoid robot into your home, but smaller connected robots are already everywhere. Robot vacuums, lawn mowers and security devices can collect video, map your property and connect to remote servers. Before you buy one, take a few minutes to check how the company protects that access.

Connected devices sold in the United States should include an FCC identification number. You can usually find it on the product, packaging or manufacturer's website. Be cautious if the company provides no clear regulatory information.
Find out whether the robot stores camera footage and room maps locally or uploads them to the cloud. The privacy policy should explain where the company stores that information and who can access it.
Turn off remote viewing or cloud controls when you do not need them. A feature that lets you control a robot from anywhere could also become an entry point for someone else.
TOP TRUMP AGENCY PURGES OVER 20 SUSPECTED CHINA-LINKED PRODUCTS FROM FEDERAL MARKETPLACE
Washington is targeting foreign-produced robots that can collect video, map sensitive locations and connect to remote cloud systems. (ADEK BERRY / AFP via Getty Images)
Robot software needs updates just like your phone or computer. Enable automatic updates when available and avoid products from companies with a poor support record.
Place connected robots and other smart devices on a guest network when your router supports it. That can help keep a compromised device away from your computers and sensitive files.

Use a strong, unique password for the account that controls your robot. A password manager can create and securely store it for you. Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) if the manufacturer offers it.

If you are installing a connected solar or battery inverter, ask the installer who can access it remotely. You should also find out how the company handles software updates and what happens if its online service shuts down.
Kurt's key takeaways

I understand why Washington is paying close attention to this. A network-connected machine with cameras and powerful motors warrants a thorough security review. That concern grows when the robot enters a factory, research center or part of America's energy infrastructure. At the same time, banning new foreign models creates a real tradeoff. Chinese companies currently build many advanced robots at prices American researchers can afford. Restricting that hardware may protect sensitive systems, but it could also slow some U.S. innovation while domestic manufacturers catch up. The success of this policy will depend on what comes next. America needs secure products, strong testing and enough domestic production to give buyers a genuine choice.
Would you accept fewer robot choices and potentially higher prices if the government said the restrictions could prevent foreign surveillance? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: KARR Bluetooth flaw exposes 2.2M cars to theft risk
summary: A Bluetooth vulnerability in dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices puts 2.2 million vehicles at risk of being unlocked by nearby attackers.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Could a small device hidden beneath your dashboard make your car easier to break into? Nancy from Newtown, Pennsylvania, asked me where she should look for the KARR or SWDS "code" in her 2025 Cadillac XT5 and 2024 Hyundai Tucson Limited Hybrid.

Here is the first thing you need to know. There is no code to find in your vehicle's settings. KARR and SWDS refer to aftermarket security hardware that a dealership may have installed before selling the car. SWDS stands for Southwest Dealer Services, the company associated with several KARR-branded vehicle protection products.
The device usually sits beneath the dashboard on the driver's side. You may also find a KARR or SWDS sticker on the driver-side window.
So, before you start searching through menus or calling the automaker, here is how to find out whether your vehicle has one of these devices and what to do next.
15 SECURITY ESSENTIALS TO KEEP YOUR VALUABLES SAFE FOR SUMMER TRAVEL

A Bluetooth flaw in dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices could expose about 2.2 million vehicles to unauthorized access. (David Baillot/University of California San Diego/Jacobs School of Engineering)
CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class "Sick of Spam?" has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.
Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
KARR Bluetooth car hack puts 2.2 million vehicles at risk

Computer security researchers at the University of California San Diego uncovered a Bluetooth vulnerability affecting at least 2.2 million vehicles. The flaw involves dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices. A person standing within about five yards of a vulnerable vehicle could connect to the device through Bluetooth.

From there, an attacker could lock or unlock the doors. The same flaw could silence the alarm, sound the horn or flash the headlights. An attacker could also prevent a parked vehicle from starting. However, the researchers did not report that the flaw could start the engine or shut down a vehicle that was already running. That distinction is important. The Bluetooth flaw alone does not let someone drive away. However, it could quietly unlock the doors. A thief could then use separate tools to create or program a key.
What are KARR and SWDS car security systems?

KARR systems are aftermarket vehicle security products sold through participating dealerships. They may include an alarm, GPS tracking, remote vehicle controls or an ignition-disabling feature. Southwest Dealer Services uses several product names, including KARR Security, KARR Fusion, KARR BT, KARR S.W.A.T. and S.W.A.T. Dealer. The features vary by product and vehicle.

These devices do not come from Cadillac, Hyundai, Ford or another automaker's factory. A dealership or one of its vendors adds the hardware after the vehicle arrives. Dealers may use the system to protect inventory sitting on the lot. When someone buys the vehicle, the dealer may offer the system as an additional security package. The problem is that some dealers left the hardware connected even when buyers declined the service. As a result, a driver might have a vulnerable device without an active KARR account or any idea that the equipment is inside the car.
How the KARR Bluetooth vulnerability works

The KARR device communicates with a smartphone app through Bluetooth Low Energy. Researchers found that the affected devices relied on the same secret authentication key. Once they recovered that key, they could send commands that vulnerable KARR devices accepted.

Think of it as giving a huge group of devices the same unchangeable password. Once that password becomes known, each device becomes easier to approach. The researchers also found that the devices broadcast recognizable Bluetooth signals. Historical databases containing those signals could reveal where a particular device had appeared. That creates a privacy concern beyond car theft. Someone could potentially use the data to study where a vehicle regularly parks or travels.
Which cars may have a KARR or SWDS device?

UC San Diego researchers found the devices most often in vehicles sold through Honda, Toyota, Mazda, Ford and Jeep dealerships in Southern California since 2017. However, that list does not mean other brands are safe.

KARR works with more than 3,000 dealerships nationwide. Vehicles also move around the country through used-car sales, auctions and dealership trades. Therefore, the vehicle's make and model cannot confirm whether it has the equipment. The dealership that prepared the vehicle for sale matters more than the badge on the grille. A Cadillac, Hyundai or Chevrolet could have a KARR system if the selling dealer installed one. A Honda from another dealership might never have received it.
How to check your car for a hidden KARR device
Start with the easy clues before you remove any trim or crawl too far beneath the dashboard.
Look at the lower corners and edges of the driver-side window.
The sticker may say:
KARRKARR Security SystemsSWDSS.W.A.T.
KARR
KARR Security Systems
SWDS
S.W.A.T.

A sticker strongly suggests that the dealership installed a related device. However, the absence of a sticker cannot completely clear your vehicle. A dealer or previous owner may have removed the label while leaving the hardware connected. UC San Diego says many affected vehicles have the sticker, rather than every affected vehicle.

Park the vehicle and shut off the engine. Move the driver's seat back and use a flashlight to look beneath the lower dashboard. Researchers say the device is usually installed underneath the dashboard on the driver's side.

You may see a small button or indicator light attached to the bottom edge of the dash. Wiring may run from the button behind the dashboard panels. The button shown by UC San Diego is small and easy to miss. It can look like a basic aftermarket alarm switch rather than a modern connected device. Do not pull on the wires or disconnect anything. The module may connect to the ignition system and other vehicle electronics.
Check the purchase agreement, dealer addendum, finance documents and service records.
Search for references to:
KARR SecurityKARR BTKARR FusionKARR S.W.A.T.SWDSSouthwest Dealer ServicesDealer alarmVehicle recovery systemInventory security system
KARR Security
KARR BT
KARR Fusion
KARR S.W.A.T.
SWDS
Southwest Dealer Services
Dealer alarm
Vehicle recovery system
Inventory security system
The charge may appear as part of a larger dealer protection package. You may also find the product listed with no separate price if the dealer installed it for inventory control.
TESLA HELPED SAVE A DRIVER; IS YOUR CAR READY?
Some Jeep, Ram and Chrysler drivers previously saw promotional messages on infotainment screens through Stellantis’ Uconnect system. (Kurt "Cyberguy" Knutsson)

Call the dealership that originally sold the vehicle. This step can help even when you bought the car used from another business. Your VIN appears near the bottom of the windshield on the driver's side. You can also find it on the registration, insurance card and driver-side door frame.
Ask the dealer: "Can you check this VIN and confirm whether your dealership or inventory vendor installed a KARR, SWDS, KARR BT, S.W.A.T. or other aftermarket security module?"

Then ask these follow-up questions: "Is the device still connected?" "Has it received the firmware update released on July 20, 2026?" "Can you provide the device model and firmware status in writing?"
A vague answer such as "Your factory alarm is fine" does not address the question. You are asking about dealer-installed aftermarket equipment.

KARR says people who never activated the security service can still use the official KARR Security app to check their VIN. Download the app only through the official Apple App Store, Google Play Store or KARR website. Do not use an app link from an unexpected text message, email or online advertisement.

After opening the app near the vehicle, tap the customer service link at the bottom of the screen. The app should guide you through the VIN check and available firmware update. KARR also lists customer support at 800-395-5277.
What Nancy should check on her Cadillac and Hyundai

Nancy's 2025 Cadillac XT5 and 2024 Hyundai Tucson Limited Hybrid were not among the specific brands UC San Diego researchers said appeared most often. However, that does not rule them out. The device comes from the dealership rather than Cadillac or Hyundai.

Nancy should check each SUV separately. First, she should look for a KARR or SWDS sticker on the driver-side window. Next, she should use a flashlight to inspect the lower edge of the dashboard near the driver's knees.

She should also review the paperwork from each dealership. If the vehicles came from different dealers, one could have the equipment while the other does not. Finally, Nancy should call both selling dealers with the VINs. She should ask whether either dealership installed a KARR, SWDS or S.W.A.T. module before delivery. If the dealers cannot provide a definite answer, she can use the official KARR app or call KARR support.
How to update a KARR security system

Acrisure released a firmware patch on July 20, 2026, one day before UC San Diego publicly announced the vulnerability. The vehicle owner must deliver the update to the KARR device through the official KARR Security app. Updating your phone or vehicle infotainment system will not patch the separate module.
An activated system means you purchased or activated KARR service through the dealership.
Follow these steps:

Go to the vehicle and sit in the driver's seat.Open the KARR Security app.Log in and select the correct vehicle.Tap the Settings button in the lower-right corner.Scroll down and tap Check for Updates.Follow the instructions shown in the app.Wait for confirmation that the firmware is current.
Go to the vehicle and sit in the driver's seat.
Open the KARR Security app.
Log in and select the correct vehicle.
Tap the Settings button in the lower-right corner.
Scroll down and tap Check for Updates.
Follow the instructions shown in the app.
Wait for confirmation that the firmware is current.
KARR says no additional action is necessary after the app confirms that the latest firmware is installed.
You can still check and update a device that remained in the vehicle after you declined the service.
Follow these steps:

Download the official KARR Security app.Sit in the driver's seat near the device.Open the app.Tap the Customer Service: 800-395-5277 link.Follow the app's instructions to check the VIN.Complete the firmware update when prompted.Confirm that the app reports the latest firmware.
Download the official KARR Security app.
Sit in the driver's seat near the device.
Open the app.
Tap the Customer Service: 800-395-5277 link.
Follow the app's instructions to check the VIN.
Complete the firmware update when prompted.
Confirm that the app reports the latest firmware.
Call KARR support when the app cannot find the vehicle or complete the update.
WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK

Drivers can check for a KARR or SWDS device by inspecting the driver-side window, dashboard area and vehicle sales paperwork. (David Baillot/University of California San Diego/Jacobs School of Engineering)
Should you remove the KARR device?

You can ask to have the system deactivated or removed. However, I would not turn this into a weekend do-it-yourself project. Researchers warn that removal may require opening the dashboard, cutting wires and restoring connections involving the ignition system or vehicle computers. Disconnecting the wrong wire could stop the car from starting. It might also affect the factory alarm, remote start or another electrical feature. Southwest Dealer Services says an owner can request removal, transfer or deactivation by calling 800-395-5277 and confirming the account information.

Ask the original dealership or a qualified automotive electrical technician to handle the work. Before approving removal, ask the technician how the factory wiring will be restored. Afterward, request written confirmation that the module was removed and the vehicle's original security functions still work.
We reached out to KARR Security, and a representative from the company provided CyberGuy with the following statement:

"KARR Security maintains rigorous standards to help protect customers’ vehicles. Researchers at UC San Diego identified a vulnerability affecting BLE-based auto theft devices, including a small percentage of KARR devices with certain Bluetooth-related components. The vulnerability described in the research is highly complex and presents a low risk to customers under real-world conditions. Nevertheless, we responded promptly and developed a firmware update to address the issue. We launched this app/firmware update on July 20, 2026. Active customers may apply the update directly from their phone after securely logging in to the KARR Security app. Vehicle owners of non-active systems can still update via the app using their VIN (last 8 digits) as a validation step. Consumers can find detailed instructions and tutorials for assistance with this firmware on the Customer FAQ section of our website at www.KARRSecurity.com."
KARR Security added, "To our knowledge, we have not seen this vulnerability used in the real world to break into or steal a vehicle."
What will not fix the KARR Bluetooth flaw

Turning off Bluetooth on your phone will not disable the Bluetooth radio inside the KARR module. Deleting the app will not remove the device. Removing the vehicle from your phone's normal Bluetooth menu will not patch it either.

The KARR module communicates separately from the Cadillac, Hyundai or other factory infotainment system. A Faraday pouch also will not fix this particular problem. Faraday pouches can help block relay attacks involving a key fob. They cannot update or disable hardware installed beneath the dashboard. You need to update the KARR device itself or have a professional remove it.
Tips to protect your vehicle from being stolen
Car thieves use different methods, so protecting your vehicle requires more than one piece of technology.

When your vehicle has a KARR or SWDS device, install the firmware update as soon as possible. This directly addresses the Bluetooth flaw identified by the researchers. A steering wheel lock or tracker can add protection, but neither one repairs vulnerable software.

Signal jammers can sometimes block the command sent by a key fob. After pressing the lock button, listen for the normal confirmation sound. Look for the lights and pull a door handle before walking away. Also, close every window and take the keys with you. NHTSA recommends checking the doors whenever you leave a parked vehicle.

A steering wheel lock creates an obvious barrier inside the car. It will not stop every determined thief. However, it adds time and makes the vehicle harder to steer. NHTSA includes steering wheel locks among visible devices that can discourage vehicle theft. You can find more ideas in my CyberGuy guide on how to help prevent your car from getting stolen.

Store key fobs away from exterior doors, windows and attached garages. A tested signal-blocking pouch can help reduce the risk of a relay attack. In that type of theft, criminals extend the signal from a key inside the house to a vehicle outside. Test the pouch regularly. Put the key inside, close the pouch and stand next to the car. The doors should remain locked when you touch the handle. Remember that a key-fob pouch protects against a different attack. It will not patch a KARR module.

A hidden GPS tracker or Bluetooth tracker may help locate a stolen vehicle. However, do not confront anyone or attempt to recover the car yourself. Give tracking information to law enforcement. An Apple AirTag can provide a backup location signal, although Apple's anti-stalking alerts may eventually warn a thief that an unknown AirTag is traveling with the vehicle. Read my CyberGuy guide on using an AirTag in a vehicle and understanding its limits.

Use a locked garage when one is available. Otherwise, park in a visible area with lighting, foot traffic or a security camera. Avoid isolated corners where someone can work around the vehicle without attracting attention. NHTSA also recommends parking in well-lit areas whenever possible.

A thief may break into a car without planning to steal the entire vehicle. Take phones, laptops, wallets and bags with you. Do not leave a spare key or garage remote inside the car. NHTSA warns that thieves commonly target electronics and other items they can quickly resell.
Kurt's key takeaways

Nancy's question highlights the biggest problem with this vulnerability. Many drivers have no idea that a KARR or SWDS device may be hiding in their vehicle. You will not find a KARR code inside your vehicle's settings. Look for a sticker on the driver-side window and a small aftermarket button below the dashboard. Then check your paperwork and ask the selling dealer to search your VIN. The flaw can unlock a vulnerable vehicle and interfere with its security features from nearby. It cannot start the engine by itself or shut down a moving car. Still, unlocking the doors may give a thief the access needed to try another method. Fortunately, KARR has released a firmware update. Install it through the official KARR Security app. When you no longer want the system, arrange professional removal rather than pulling wires yourself.
Should dealerships have to tell you about every connected device installed in your car, even when you decline to purchase the service? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.
